f4b4bb981e:4ee0b7b156ddef32.title: The Lure of the Aria
f4b4bb981e:4ee0b7b156ddef32.summary: For its fall digital issue, the Loyola Marimount University (LMU) Magazine invited readers to discover opera through a personal, playful guide written by David Davila. The article moves from beloved classics to bold contemporary works, and it dismantles the idea that opera is elitist or out of reach. Opera descends from the communal pleasure of telling stories through music, and it is for everyone. Working under the art direction of Pentagram Austin, I approached the illustrations from the same place: people. Opera is, at its core, a human art form, made of desire, jealousy, grief, humor, and defiance. Rather than depicting grand stages or spectacle, I looked for the intimate moments inside each story, the glance, the gesture, the expression that tells you what a character is feeling before they sing a note. f4b4bb981e:140e76cbca592c2f.title: BAROQUE BIOLOGY
f4b4bb981e:140e76cbca592c2f.summary: If you closely observe the genetics of any living being, you'll see everything is much more baroque than functional. Midway between perfecting and contaminating, aesthetics refuse to be domesticated. Biology, like creativity, is immensely messy, caught in the constant cycle of decay, regeneration and return. Baroque Biology is a curated selection of Alex Valentina's works that explores these primordial concepts. Like remnants found on a beach, the elements in all these pieces carry the scent of the sea and subsoil ? rarities like pearls and strange shells that appear precious to the human eye, yet are merely discarded matter to nature. Like an island left to its own flow, here the aesthetics of decomposing natural elements speak of life and regeneration, as if each new idea breathes fresh life into all those that came before it. Biological creativity will endure, no matter what happens.

Its unconventional structure reflects the spontaneous nature of creative thinking, where ideas emerge, overlap and take unexpected directions. This approach became the foundation for the packaging design. A vivid orange palette creates an expressive and instantly recognizable visual presence. The wordmark is enhanced with a dimensional 3D finish, turning typography into a tactile element that extends beyond the printed surface. The result is a visual identity that feels energetic, unconventional and unapologetically bold. SKELTCH transforms everyday stationery into an expression of creativity, where even the simplest blank page holds the potential for something new.

a4977d3fa4:09f22028b47c1be5.title: The Nike Mind 001 Sets Its Moving Nodes in Chocolate Brown for "Palomino"
a4977d3fa4:09f22028b47c1be5.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:09f22028b47c1be5.summary: Name: Nike Mind 001 “Palomino”Colorway: Palomino/Tar-Metallic PlatinumSKU: HQ4307-201MSRP: $95 USDRelease Date: Spring 2027The Nike Mind 001 "Palomino" is set to give one of Nike's more experimental silhouettes an earthy update, with a palette built from olive, brown and flashes of metallic platinum. According to early details, the build is focused on how the shoe connects you to the ground, and Nike frames the design around feeling every surface and staying aware of each step.From the side, olive does most of the work. It covers much of the profile and continues down to the wavy edge of the sole, while brown tones take over higher on the upper. A perforated panel in light brown runs from the collar almost to the toe and carries a small metallic silver Swoosh in its center. A second Swoosh stands upright on the outside of the molded shell for a bolder branding moment.The outsole is where the Mind 001 stands apart. Twenty-two chocolate brown nodes are spread across the bottom, and each one moves on its own as you walk, so the sole adjusts to whatever is under it instead of acting as one rigid platform. That setup is central to Nike's pitch for the shoe, which centers on ground feel and a more deliberate stride.Nike also adds a playful detail inside. The footbeds don't match: one carries "Nike Mind" in white lettering, and the other reads "Mind Science Department," which points back to the research-lab theme behind the line.Set your reminders and get ahead of what’s dropping next on Hypebeast Drops. a4977d3fa4:f4522a9735aaa0d2.title: Panini Turns ‘GTA VI's’ In-Game Collectibles Into a Real Sports Trading Card Collection
a4977d3fa4:f4522a9735aaa0d2.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f4522a9735aaa0d2.summary: Summary Panini America and Rockstar Games are releasing the ‘GTA VI’ Sports Trading Card Collection, their first trading card tie-in for the gameThe officially licensed set turns the collectible cards found inside ‘GTA VI’ into physical cardsParallels range from Special Silver, Pink, Teal and Light Blue up to numbered Legend Bronze, Silver and 1-of-1 Gold cards Panini America and Rockstar Games are launching the GTA VI Sports Trading Card Collection, a licensed set that takes the card collectibles players chase in Grand Theft Auto VI and puts them into physical packs. It's the first trading card partnership built around the game, so collectors can open real packs of the same cards that show up in-game.Each box holds four packs and is built to give a predictable spread of base hits. On average, a box yields two Rookies, one Retro and one Illustrated card, plus four Special Silvers, so every rip covers the set's main card styles. With the Rookies, Retros and Illustrated cards working as distinct subsets, collectors have a clear checklist to work through before the parallel hunt begins.The parallels are where the chase gets serious. Beyond Special Silver, the set comes in Pink, Teal and Light Blue versions for collectors building rainbows. The numbered tiers then narrow quickly: Legend Bronze is limited to 49 copies, Silver drops to 25, and the Gold parallels are true 1-of-1s, making them the hardest cards in the set to pull.The GTA VI Sports Trading Card Collection from Panini America and Rockstar Games is set to release in December 2026. a4977d3fa4:4c2612daf1551b54.title: Lil Uzi Vert Weaves a Rainbow of Thread Into the Vans Authentic 44 "Pink Cosmos"
a4977d3fa4:4c2612daf1551b54.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:4c2612daf1551b54.summary: Name: Lil Uzi Vert x Vans Authentic 44 “Pink Cosmos”Colorway: Pink/Multi-ColorSKU: VN0010WY3TDMSRP: TBCRelease Date: Holiday 2026Lil Uzi Vert's Vans Authentic 44 "Pink Cosmos" is reportedly set to close out the year, giving one of the label's most pared-back silhouettes a heavily textured finish. The pair arrives as the rapper steps back into the spotlight with new music, so his latest era comes with footwear to match.The upper is made from a dense weave of multicolored threads. So many shades are packed in that the surface reads as tactile rather than printed, and it changes depending on how close you look. Pink is the loudest of the bunch, and it doesn't stay in the weave. It runs onto the eyelets and wraps the ankle collar, so the colorway holds together from toe to heel.Branding is kept to a few deliberate touches, which leaves most of the work to the woven upper. Inside, the insole carries a Vans logo with a "By Lil Uzi Vert" credit tucked underneath. A second Vans logo on the heel bumper anchors the back of the shoe.That restraint suits a silhouette that has always been about simplicity. The Authentic began as Style 44, the canvas deck shoe the Van Doren Rubber Company sold when it opened in Anaheim, California, in 1966. Skaters later adopted it for its grippy waffle outsole, and that makes 2026 the model's 60th year. A woven, pink-forward reading of it is a deliberate departure from the plain canvas the shoe built its name on.The pink is no accident either. The color has become a calling card for Uzi, most visibly through his 2023 album Pink Tape, and his wardrobe has long ignored the usual lines between menswear and womenswear. His ties to Vans go back to at least May 2025, when he fronted the label's Premium Old Skool campaign. Earlier this year he teased further collaborative designs online, including a pink and black checkerboard Slip-On and several takes on the chunky Lynzie skate shoe. Against those louder pieces, the Authentic is the most wearable…

a4977d3fa4:40969e8f1a3eb473.title: Apple Is Reportedly Planning an M6 MacBook Air Refresh for Spring 2027 Ahead of an OLED Redesign
a4977d3fa4:40969e8f1a3eb473.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:40969e8f1a3eb473.summary: Summary Apple is preparing a dual-phase rollout for the MacBook Air, starting with an M6 chip update in spring 2027The initial launch will be a straightforward spec refresh, arriving alongside the new MacBook Neo 2A major design overhaul featuring an OLED display is slated to follow in late 2027 or 2028 During a Thanksgiving mailbag episode of his Power On podcast, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman fielded a listener Q&A segment that laid out the immediate roadmap for Apple’s most popular laptop. Titled "Mailbag: Mark Answers Your Questions About Apple’s Product & Political Future," the episode detailed major two-part release plans for the MacBook Air. According to Gurman, Apple is planning to launch new 13-inch and 15-inch iterations of the machine in spring 2027. Developed internally under the project codenames J913 and J915, these forthcoming models will officially introduce Apple's M6 chip to the lightweight laptop line. However, the spring drop isn't meant to reinvent the wheel. Gurman specifically described this spring 2027 release as a straightforward "chip and ship" refresh that brings minimal hardware changes to the table.When these M6-powered MacBook Air models hit the market, they are scheduled to launch right alongside an entirely new device known as the MacBook Neo 2. But while the internals are getting a performance boost, the exterior of the current generation is rapidly aging out. Gurman noted on the podcast that the current MacBook Air aesthetic is nearing the "end of the road." Apple originally introduced this specific industrial design language back in 2022 and updated the line by adding a larger 15-inch model to the roster in 2023.Because the MacBook Air is currently Apple's most popular computer, heavy pressure remains on the company to keep its hardware designs fresh and relevant. To answer that demand, Apple is aggressively developing a major design overhaul for the lineup, slated for release in late 2027 at the earliest, or potentially…

a4977d3fa4:f9dccd0d40e23473.title: Maison Kitsuné and Paraboot Rework the Classic Chambord for Fall/Winter 2026
a4977d3fa4:f9dccd0d40e23473.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f9dccd0d40e23473.summary: Summary Maison Kitsuné and Paraboot reunite to reinterpret the classic Chambord derby.Glossy brown leather pairs with white contrast stitching and asymmetrical logo tabs.Priced at approx. $670 USD, it launches November 28 in limited quantities. Name: Maison Kitsuné x Paraboot “Chambord”Colorway: BrownSKU: TBCMSRP: ¥106,700 JPY (approx. $670 USD)Release Date: November 28Where to Buy: Maison KitsunéMaison Kitsuné and Paraboot have reunited for their second footwear collaboration. First previewed as part of Maison Kitsuné’s Fall/Winter 2026 collection, the release sees the duo reinterpret Paraboot’s signature Chambord derby, taking the French brand’s silhouette and reframing it through a casual preppy lens.Built around the Chambord’s rounded U-tip paneling, the shoe uses glossy brown leather rich with tonal shading. Crisp white stitching traces the contours and runs across the upper at a 45-degree angle, sharpening the silhouette’s three-dimensional form against the deep-toned hide. The defining touch sits on the side: Paraboot’s signature green tag is split asymmetrically across the pair, placing the shoemaker’s logo on the right foot and Maison Kitsuné’s fox emblem on the left.Rather than reinventing the wheel, the two labels opted to highlight heritage craftsmanship and designed the shoe to blend naturally into everyday outfits. Offered in limited quantities, the shoe launches November 28 via Maison Kitsuné’s online store and select Japanese locations. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:5316589b4ee2015d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5316589b4ee2015d.summary: Summary Y-3 and Jeff Hamilton create a custom jacket for Kimi Antonelli’s first F1 Drivers' World Champion title.The quilted black piece features stripes, Italian accents, and championship graphics.Made exclusively for Antonelli, the bespoke tribute won’t release publicly. Marking a defining milestone in Kimi Antonelli’s career, Y-3 and Jeff Hamilton have unveiled a one-of-one jacket created exclusively for the driver to celebrate his first Formula 1 Drivers’ World Championship win with the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team.Turning his achievement into a wearable trophy, the custom piece arrives in a sleek black quilted silhouette with a structured hood, featuring bold contrasting white stripes down the sleeves alongside checkered detailing. Co-branded Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team and Y-3 logos sit cleanly across the chest, while personalized touches — including red “ANTONELLI” lettering and the Italian tricolor flag along the sleeve — serve as a direct nod to the champion’s heritage. A prominent “2026 F1 World Champion” graphic spans the back, placing his win squarely at the center of the design.Built purely as a personal tribute to Antonelli’s championship-winning season, the bespoke jacket is not slated for a public release. a4977d3fa4:129e6fa59a998c15.title: Moncler x Rick Owens FW26 Arms Quilted Outerwear With Studs and Straps
a4977d3fa4:129e6fa59a998c15.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:129e6fa59a998c15.summary: Summary Moncler and Rick Owens return with a Fall/Winter 2026 collection built mainly around quilted outerwearGeo Quilting, metal studs, oversized Tour pockets and a carry-ready Mega Strap appear across the lineupThe collection uses a tight palette of black, metallic Palladium, Cloud Grey and a muted Grease tone The Moncler x Rick Owens Fall/Winter 2026 collection is built around outerwear. It brings Owens' subversive eye together with the Italian house's background in warm, protective technical gear. The two labels have shaped each other's work over time, and this season puts that exchange into a run of quilted pieces in a wide range of shapes.Quilting is the collection's backbone. A graphic Geo Quilting pattern breaks up the surfaces into sharp, architectural sections, so even the simpler shapes have an edge. Owens' hardware sits on top: metal studs run along the outerwear, and oversized Tour pockets add real storage without diluting the look.The most practical detail is the Mega Strap. It's a large carrying strap that lets you sling a jacket over your shoulder or across your body when you've taken it off, so heavy layers don't have to be either worn or left behind. It's a small change, but it makes these voluminous pieces easier to get through a day of changing temperatures with.The palette stays restrained so the textures stand out. Black anchors the range, and metallic Palladium adds a liquid shine, Cloud Grey softens the mix and Grease gives a quieter, lived-in tone. The pieces are designed to be layered from head to toe, and Thyra sunglasses and Trailgrip Pentalace ankle boots complete the looks.Owens photographed the campaign himself and cast Joe Dallesandro, the cult star of Warhol-era underground film, who wears the collection's biggest shapes in black and white. The designer explained the choice by pointing to Dallesandro's link to Lou Reed. "Little Joe mythologized an indifferent beauty in Lou Reed's hymn to queer subculture. 'Take a Walk on the Wild…

a4977d3fa4:d0fdde07569cdbf7.title: The Clock Starts Again as ‘The Pitt’ Season 3 Locks Its Premiere Date
a4977d3fa4:d0fdde07569cdbf7.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:d0fdde07569cdbf7.summary: Summary 'The Pitt' returns to HBO Max for Season 3 on January 7, keeping its usual early-January premiere slotNoah Wyle leads a returning cast that includes Patrick Ball, Katherine LaNasa, Fiona Dourif and Shawn HatosyThe medical drama has won 12 Emmy Awards from 38 nominations across its first two seasons HBO Max has set January 7, 2027 as the premiere date for The Pitt Season 3, bringing the Emmy-winning medical drama back to the emergency room for another year. The date keeps the show in the early-January slot it has held since its debut, when Season 1 premiered on January 9, 2025, and Season 2 followed on January 8, 2026.The core of the Pittsburgh trauma center is returning. Noah Wyle again plays Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch, with Patrick Ball as Dr. Langdon, Katherine LaNasa as charge nurse Dana Evans and Fiona Dourif as Dr. McKay. Taylor Dearden (Dr. King), Isa Briones (Dr. Santos), Gerran Howell (Dr. Whitaker) and Shabana Azeez (Javadi) are also back. Ayesha Harris returns as Dr. Ellis, alongside Sepideh Moafi as Dr. Al-Hashimi and Shawn Hatosy as Dr. Abbot.One face won't be back on the floor. Supriya Ganesh, who played senior resident Dr. Samira Mohan, left the series ahead of Season 3. Her exit opens a gap in the residency ranks that the new season will have to work around.The creative team hasn't changed. R. Scott Gemmill created the show and executive produces with John Wells through John Wells Productions, alongside Wyle, Michael Hissrich, Erin Jontow, Joe Sachs, Simran Baidwan and Eli Attie. The series' official logline describes it as "a realistic examination of the challenges facing healthcare workers in today's America as seen through the lens of the frontline heroes working in a modern-day hospital in Pittsburgh."That focus on realism has paid off. Across its first two seasons, The Pitt has collected 12 Emmy Awards from 38 nominations, including consecutive wins for Outstanding Drama Series and for Wyle as Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama…

a4977d3fa4:3f8ef7ddc0007617.title: Porsche Brings Mid-Engine DNA to the EV Era With the All-Electric 718 Boxster
a4977d3fa4:3f8ef7ddc0007617.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:3f8ef7ddc0007617.summary: Summary Porsche’s first all-electric 718 Boxster debuts in Q1 2027.Bespoke E-Core architecture and 911 hardware preserve mid-engine balance.The rear-wheel-drive flagship hits 60 mph in under three seconds with simulated seven-speed shifts. Porsche is nearing the finish line with its first all-electric two-door sports car, confirming that the production-ready 718 Boxster will make its world premiere in the first quarter of 2027 following nearly 2.5 million miles of endurance testing across more than 20 countries. Structurally, the 718 Boxster utilizes a bespoke E-Core architecture designed to preserve classic sports car proportions. Mounting its 800-volt battery directly behind the seats allows the car to retain a low seating position and a traditional 40:60 front-to-rear weight distribution, while lightweight construction keeps overall weight similar to the current 911 Cabriolet T-Hybrid. Underneath, the roadster borrows heavily from its big brother, the 911, with Carrera GTS-based steering, 911-derived brakes, an electronically controlled PTV+ limited-slip differential, and rear-axle steering—available on the 718 Boxster for the first time. The all-electric 718 Boxster will be the most powerful 718 ever, exclusively featuring rear-wheel drive. The flagship variant accelerates from 0 to 60 mph in under three seconds and reaches a top track speed in excess of 155 mph. Standard E-Shift technology adds an analog feel back into the driving experience by simulating a seven-speed PDK transmission with automatic or paddle-operated shifts, accompanied by the familiar six-cylinder boxer soundtrack based on the 981 Boxster GTS. Production will take place at Porsche’s Stuttgart-Zuffenhausen plant. While exact output, range, and pricing remain under wraps, enthusiasts can rest assured that the all-electric 718 Boxster still has Porsche DNA coursing through its veins. a4977d3fa4:a980aa479b0703db.title: NANGA to Host Limited-Time Pop-Up Store in New York
a4977d3fa4:a980aa479b0703db.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)

a4977d3fa4:0bd8ce4b2468a3c3.title: Infinix Packs Its ZClip 2 Pro Earbuds Into a Snack Bag
a4977d3fa4:0bd8ce4b2468a3c3.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:0bd8ce4b2468a3c3.summary: The Infinix ZClip 2 Pro comes in a foil snack pouch, a form familiar to all. Tear the notched edge, hear the crinkle, and instead of chips you get a pair of metallic open-ear earbuds.The ZClip 2 Pro ships in air-filled foil pouches modeled on real snack packaging. The thinking is simple. Snacks and earbuds are two of the easiest everyday escapes, so Infinix put one inside the other and turned unboxing into a small reward ritual. Infinix calls it "Snack Aesthetics," and for a social-first generation that shares everything it opens. Where the industry keeps packaging quiet and serious, Infinix makes it loud and playful. The brand brings a sense of delight to everyday tech products through fun packaging and unboxing experiences.Each foil pouch is fronted by one of three art-toy characters, blending distinct style personas with playful snack pairings. The Streetwise Gorilla, wearing a street jersey and gold chains, channels the bold, loud crunch of spicy chips. The High-Fashion Black Rabbit wears a dark leather jacket, evoking the smooth bite of premium dark chocolate. Finally, the Laid-back Sheep pairs vintage leather with retro shades, matching the relaxed comfort of a classic sweet puff. Beyond driving the packaging's visual style, their distinct features: the gorilla's human-like ears, the rabbit's tall points, and the sheep's floppy drop, demonstrate what Infinix calls its universal "All-Ear Fit."The pouch is only the first step. The same idea carries through the whole campaign, built around "Clip on, drift away". Opening a snack and clipping on a pair of earbuds are both quick ways to step out of a busy day, and Infinix takes that idea out of the packaging and into the city. To launch the ZClip 2 Pro, Infinix turned ride-hailing cars into small mobile sanctuaries. Inside, passengers found plants, soft warm lighting, shelves of snacks and the new earbuds. a4977d3fa4:0837a784db4de695.summary: The Tulum jungle in Mexico has been integral to Zamna’s rise, hosting its first music festival back in 2017. Though the culture and hospitality group has taken the festival to over 20 countries since its inception, it returns to its roots for Zamna’s 10th anniversary with a special 10-day line-up in the ancient area. Teasing global festival-goers, Zamna launched a commemorative film last week, which captured celebrations from the last decade. From high-octane sets by renowned DJs Peggy Gou and David Guetta to theatrical productions that gave a stage to Tale Of Us, Rüfüs du Sol, and Gorillaz, the visuals traced iconic moments that fed off the “land, culture and history” to shape a festival that connects people and platforms dance music. For the upcoming 10th anniversary event, the group continues to cement itself as a global destination for dance culture. Turning the programming up a notch, the schedule kicks off on New Year’s Eve with a takeover from British electronic music platform RENAISSANCE. After welcoming Sasha, Maceo Plex, and Ida Engberg to the festival, Amnesia makes its Zamna debut, bringing a piece of Ibiza to Mexico for its own milestone anniversary. Other curated line-ups include ANYMA’s Berlin club night ÆDEN, Adriatique’s X, and Black Coffee, culminating with a special showcase from Adam Port of Keinemusik. Alongside announcing the full line-up, Zamna has also revealed it will be partnering with UMusic Hotel and Beach Club in Tulum for the anniversary festival. Having built its local presence through collaborations with nearby institutions, Zamna’s latest partnership will elevate its efforts in hospitality by introducing a VIP experience at the property. Attendees will be able to flow from the festival space to the hotel with a new multipass, while also getting to visit special Zamna events there all year round. “For us, it has always been about the people. a4977d3fa4:1e20631925b25255.title: LISA Gives The Nike Zoom Streak 3 "Black/Red" an Early Debut at the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix

Appearing alongside drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, she gave the public its first look at a colorway from the Zoom Streak 3 collection due in Spring 2027.The Zoom Streak 3 was built for racing, and its construction reflects that. A one-piece mesh upper keeps weight to a minimum and cuts down on overlays, while a Cushlon midsole provides responsive, low-profile cushioning. A Zoom Air unit in the heel adds impact protection without making the shoe heavier, a balance of lightness and performance that made the model a favorite among Nike athletes after its 2009 debut.The shoe's racing record backs up that reputation. Between 2009 and 2013, no earlier Nike racing shoe had been worn across more finish lines than the Zoom Streak 3, which made it one of the brand's most successful racing flats. Now Nike is pulling it from the archive and repositioning the low-slung silhouette as an everyday sneaker, and the Black/Red colorway gives it a sharp, high-contrast look.The setting for the reveal was deliberate. a4977d3fa4:9011954778c8d55b.title: Blancpain Unveils New Watch Featuring the World's First 30-Degree Inclined One-Minute Flying Carrousel
a4977d3fa4:9011954778c8d55b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:9011954778c8d55b.summary: Blancpain, the world's oldest watch brand founded in Villeret, Switzerland in 1735, has announced a new watch, the Tourbillon Carrousel Inclined. Completed after four years of development, this model features what the brand claims to be the world's first one-minute flying carrousel inclined at 30 degrees.The carrousel is a mechanism designed to minimize the rate variations caused by the orientation of the watch. By housing the balance wheel and escapement—which regulate the timekeeping—in a rotating cage, it averages out the effects of gravity. In 2008, Blancpain introduced a wristwatch equipped with a flying carrousel whose cage makes one full rotation per minute. For this new release, tilting the rotation axis of that cage by 30 degrees ensures that the orientation of the balance wheel continues to change relative to gravity even when the watch is laid flat with the dial facing up.During development, multiple inclination angles from 0 to 35 degrees were tested, measuring amplitude and rate across six different positions. As a result, 30 degrees was adopted as the angle that best balances precision performance, movement thinness, and design. The newly developed manual-winding Calibre 222ISQ secures a 100-hour power reserve via two series-connected barrels. Furthermore, every piece comes with an individual chronometry certificate showing an average daily rate tolerance between 0 and +2 seconds.The exterior also boasts a major distinguishing feature. It adopts Blancpain's first-ever full sapphire case, with sapphire also used for the dial. The movement's action can be admired not just from the front, but from the back and sides as well. The entire movement has been thoroughly skeletonized so that normally hidden gears, barrels, and even the winding state of the mainspring are visible.The case is available in two versions: 5N red gold and rhodium-plated gold. The 30-degree inclined complication is housed within relatively compact dimensions of 40.30 mm in diameter…

a4977d3fa4:a4aaf22c72ccb498.title: Starbucks Japan Launches the Potato Soupaccino, a Half-Soup, Half-Cappuccino Winter Drink

a4977d3fa4:a4aaf22c72ccb498.summary: Summary Starbucks Japan introduces the Potato Soupaccino as a half-soup, half-cappuccino hybrid beverage for the winter seasonThe savory comfort drink features a potato, caramelized onion and sweet vegetable flavor profile topped with customizable foamThe exclusive seasonal release continues a regional trend of savory coffee alternatives that are not launching in the United States Starbucks Japan launched its unconventional winter offering, the Potato Soupaccino, on November 13. The menu item is a half-soup, half-cappuccino hybrid beverage that blurs the line between a traditional hot drink and a savory comfort meal. By launching this savory option, the brand continues a regional trend of offering exclusive winter coffee alternatives that bypass Western menus.For this winter season, Starbucks added a potato flavor to the lineup to create a profile rooted in culinary comfort. The Potato Soupaccino features a pillowy texture reminiscent of freshly baked potatoes. To build the flavor profile, the recipe combines an earthy potato base with caramelized onions and subtle notes of sweet vegetables.The preparation process embraces a traditional coffeehouse aesthetic. Starbucks baristas finish the drink by adding a frothy layer of cappuccino foam on top of the savory base. Customers can choose their preferred milk variety for the foam layer to customize the beverage.The new potato flavor expands on the savory hybrid concept that Starbucks Japan introduced in 2025 with truffle and pumpkin flavors. This evolution demonstrates how Starbucks Japan establishes its seasonal lineup as a permanent space for experimental savory coffee alternatives rather than standard sweet syrups. a4977d3fa4:646a23eab1bcb697.title: BIRKENSTOCK Celebrates the 40th Anniversary of Its Iconic London Style with the "Camden's Clubs" Collection

a4977d3fa4:646a23eab1bcb697.summary: German footwear brand BIRKENSTOCK has unveiled "1774 Camden's Clubs," a new collection inspired by London's music, fashion, and subcultures. Building on four of the brand's signature models—the Arizona, London, Boston, and Maria—the collection features silver cone studs and glossy brushed leather. It adds a rebellious edge evocative of punk and grunge to classic silhouettes.The collection takes its name from the legendary music clubs scattered throughout London's Camden neighborhood. It focuses on the city's creative soil, where music, fashion, and various subcultures have intersected from King's Road to Camden.This is rooted in the London youth culture of the early 1990s. Around Camden Lock at the time, grunge, hippie, and romantic styles mixed. It was common to see outfits layering delicate materials like lace and chiffon paired with rugged boots or BIRKENSTOCK clogs. The unique contrast created by boldly combining different tastes was a signature style of London in that era.In a 1993 article for *The New York Times*, fashion journalist Suzy Menkes also highlighted the hippie style revival at Camden Lock. She described outfits that paired lightweight fabrics like lace skirts and chiffon blouses with heavy stockings, Dr. Martens boots, and BIRKENSTOCK clogs. This collection can be seen as a modern reinterpretation of the fashion scene of that time, where these contrasting elements coexisted.A standout in the collection is the London, which celebrates its 40th anniversary this year. Introduced in 1986 by Karl Birkenstock, it was the brand's first shoe to cover both the toe and heel. a4977d3fa4:9803a2c948ab00f4.summary: Summary Ki One Whisky Distillery won the IWSC 2026 Worldwide Whiskey Producer Trophy, an award given to a distillery's whole range rather than a single bottleTo make the shortlist, a producer has to enter at least three products, medal with every one and take at least two GoldsKi One went eight for eight on medals, with Ki One Eagle and Ki One Moon both winning Gold Ki One Whisky Distillery has won the Worldwide Whiskey Producer Trophy at the IWSC 2026 Awards Ceremony, held November 24 at Outernet Live in London. The Namyangju-based distillery is the first from Korea to be shortlisted for the trophy and the first to win it. The award comes a year after Ki One Unicorn took the competition's top single-bottle honor, the Worldwide Whiskey Trophy.The format of the Producer Trophy is what makes the win significant, because it judges a distillery's whole output rather than its single best bottle. Producers only reach the shortlist if they enter three or more products in the category, every one of those entries wins a medal, and at least two of the medals are Gold. The IWSC judging committee then reviews the finalists and picks a winner based on overall medal performance and the results of Trophy Judging.Ki One cleared that bar comfortably this year. It entered eight whiskies and every one came away with a medal, including Golds for Ki One Eagle and Ki One Moon. The entries were judged double-blind by a panel drawn from more than 30 countries, as part of a competition that takes in around 5,000 wine and spirits entries from roughly 90 countries each year.The shortlist also included Kavalan and Wan Ja Shan from Taiwan, The Lakes from England, Laizhou from China and Archie Rose from Australia. Redbreast from Ireland and Kavalan have both won the trophy before.Ki One's approach to entering builds on the strategy behind last year's result. a4977d3fa4:76abc5d1657bc10e.title: Rare Hilma af Klint Masterpiece Commands a Record-Breaking $12.7 Million USD at Auction
a4977d3fa4:76abc5d1657bc10e.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:76abc5d1657bc10e.summary: Summary A 1920 abstract painting by pioneering artist Hilma af Klint recently sold for a record-breaking $12.7 million USD at a Swedish auction houseThe rare offering of 'Ser III No. 5' marks a historic moment for the artist whose foundation typically keeps her work strictly off the marketThe unprecedented sale sparked controversy among art historians who argue the esoteric work was never intended for commercial consumption Pioneering artist Hilma af Klint has set a new posthumous record following the landmark sale of her 1920 abstraction, Ser III No. 5. Hosted by the Bukowskis auction house in Stockholm, the extremely rare market appearance resulted in a staggering $12.7 million USD final price, a sum roughly 15 times its initial high estimate of $800,000 USD.Held closely by a single unnamed family since 1995, the painting was originally acquired after the artist's foundation deaccessioned a small number of works. The sale adds a lucrative new chapter to af Klint's posthumous ascent. While the artist remained relatively obscure following her death in 1944, a series of blockbuster museum exhibitions in the 2010s—including a record-shattering 2018 showcase at the New York Guggenheim Museum—firmly repositioned her as a foundational inventor of European abstraction. Her enigmatic canvases, featuring dazzling arrays of curlicuing lines and inscrutable symbols, were famously created in response to spirits she contacted.Because the foundation generally restricts her artwork from entering the commercial market, the recent Bukowskis auction sparked debate among art historians. Critics of the sale, including af Klint scholar Rachel Villari, argued that placing a price tag on the esoteric works contradicts the artist's original intentions and removes culturally significant pieces from public access. Despite the pushback, the auction house celebrated the historic hammer price, with CEO Louise Arén noting that simply selling an abstract work by af Klint is a remarkable feat…

a4977d3fa4:414d405070ab1a5a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:414d405070ab1a5a.summary: Summary ESPN's telecast of Super Bowl LXI will screen live in hundreds of IMAX theaters on February 14, 2027, the first time the game has ever reached the formatThe four-hour-plus presentation covers pregame, the full game, the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show headlined by JAY-Z and postgame analysisScreenings span the US, Australia, New Zealand and Brazil, with the 'Monday Night Football' booth calling the action ESPN, The Walt Disney Company, the NFL and IMAX are taking Super Bowl LXI to the big screen, with ESPN's live telecast set to play across hundreds of IMAX theaters on February 14, 2027. It's the first time the Super Bowl has ever been shown in IMAX, and the partners are billing it as the largest live event the company has hosted. The screening lands in the same season as another milestone, since Super Bowl LXI is also the first Super Bowl ESPN has produced in its 47-year history.The theatrical feed mirrors what viewers at home will see, starting at 6 p.m. ET and running for more than four hours as a one-day-only event. The full package covers pregame coverage, ESPN's main game telecast, the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show with 25-time GRAMMY winner JAY-Z, and postgame analysis. The Monday Night Football crew of Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Lisa Salters and Laura Rutledge will call the game.Hundreds of IMAX locations across the US will carry the broadcast, and Australia, New Zealand and Brazil are also confirmed. The exact theater count hasn't been announced yet, and a list of participating locations is set to arrive in the coming weeks. For IMAX, the Super Bowl is its largest test so far as a venue for live programming. IMAX CEO Rich Gelfond said in the announcement that the game is "a one-of-a-kind global cultural event imbued with spectacle, sound, drama, and heroes ... all the makings of a great IMAX experience.""Watching the Super Bowl with your fellow fans is one of the great shared experiences in sports, and this first-of-its-kind…

a4977d3fa4:2779f3cab94b3db0.summary: Leading Japanese outdoor brand Snow Peak is releasing a new wood-burning stove, the Arma Stove (ST-210). d006da4fe3:cccd877b2427dfd1.author: Charles Kupchan
d006da4fe3:cccd877b2427dfd1.summary: In just a few days’ time, U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin could be holding a three-way summit on the sidelines of next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen, China. According to The Wall Street Journal, Putin floated the idea of a trialogue last month as an opportunity to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. No firm plan has yet been announced, but even the prospect of this meeting has provoked widespread consternation. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski warned against a repeat of the Yalta Conference of 1945, when U.S. President Franklin Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill capitulated to Soviet leader Joseph Stalin’s push for the Soviet Union to dominate Eastern Europe. U.S. Senator Chris Coons wrote on X that “There can be no talks about Ukraine’s future without Ukraine at the table, and there can be no real negotiations as long as Trump signals weakness and servitude to Xi and Putin at every opportunity.”

d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.title: America’s AI Ambitions Depend on Taiwan
d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.author: Lin Chia-lung
d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.summary: The United States and China are locked in a global competition to determine who will dominate artificial intelligence and whether it will be democracies or autocracies that set the standards and values of the new digital age. The United States leads the world in the sophistication and power of its artificial intelligence models, and its innovation base and investment in research and development remain unparalleled.But AI competition is much broader than modeling alone. It encompasses a technology ecosystem that includes power generation, servers, and deployment in real-world applications. Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia, has described the AI industry as a five-layer cake with energy at its base and chips, infrastructure, models, and applications above it. To win the AI race with China, the United States needs to maintain or establish an advantage in each of these layers. And to do that, the United States needs Taiwan.

d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.summary: Tatiana Mitrova, a fellow at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy and former energy scholar at Moscow’s Russian Academy of Sciences, and Sergey Vakulenko, an oil and gas expert at Carnegie’s Russia Eurasia Center, argue that Russia and Ukraine are locked in an energy war that has become an adaptation spiral, despite growing human and economic costs and despite current US pressure on Ukraine. They observe Ukraine’s remarkable ability to withstand Russian strikes, while questioning claims that long-range Ukrainian strikes will be able to achieve game-changing damage on Russia. Ukraine and Russia have transformed the role of energy warfare in modern conflict, drawing on low costs drones but also new forms of technological resilience that are likely to make wars longer and more dangerous.

d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.title: The China Price
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.author: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.summary: In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally told a group of worried European finance ministers that the dollar was “our currency, but your problem.” The dollar had become that system’s official reserve currency in 1944, under the Bretton Woods agreement, making signatories subject to the whims of U.S. monetary policy. Even after Bretton Woods collapsed and many currencies floated freely, the dollar continued to dominate. In the last half century, U.S. currency power has only expanded, as more countries have integrated into the global economy and therefore grown to depend on the dollar. China, reliant on export-driven growth, is foremost among them.

d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.summary: The advent of a new technology invariably comes with strategic implications, raising the question of who will benefit and whether risks can be managed. The United States could not risk losing out, Berkner argued, but nor should governments allow geopolitical tensions to prevent the technology’s broad benefits from emerging.

fc066e842d:b3b626021a74ed1b.title: Innovation partnerships for development along green value chains
fc066e842d:b3b626021a74ed1b.author: Verhoeven, Dennis
fc066e842d:b3b626021a74ed1b.summary: Growth and development success stories are often linked to new technological waves and innovation success. Green technologies emerge as a new technology category in which innovation quality in Emerging and Developing Economies (EMDE) - even when excluding China - is relatively high when measured via the value of knowledge spillovers they generate. This suggests that further R&D investment in developing country green-tech could be growth-enhancing. How could this be funded? We show that the highest-impact developing-country innovations are produced in collaborations between developing-country innovators and firms or innovators in High-Income Countries (HIC). Indeed, such collaborations, while amounting to only about 2% of HIC innovations, account for nearly half of all EMDE innovations. We also find that more diversified firms, with R&D staff from both HIC and EMDE, generate more knowledge spillovers in both EMDE and HIC. We suggest a model of innovation where the likelihood of a successful innovation is enhanced by more diverse but complementary knowledge stocks. Our results suggest that observed diversification is likely well below optimal levels and could be enhanced by policies such as tax breaks for R&D in EMDE or co-investments by development banks.

fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.title: Intangible Capital as a Source of Economic Growth and Productivity: A Literature Review and Policy Guidelines
fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.author: Rouvinen, Petri
fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.summary: Abstract This review synthesizes the latest scholarly evidence on intangible capital. Drawing on 60 recent studies across macro, meso, and micro levels (anchored by firm-level data from Finland, broader Europe, the US, and Asia) it demonstrates that intangible investments have emerged as the preeminent engine of economic growth, competitiveness, and productivity. The literature yields three critical imperatives for public policy. First, the measurement and statistical tracking of intangibles require a fundamental overhaul; at present, a swath of these investments remains invisible in official data and absent from corporate balance sheets. Second, policymakers must broaden their horizons beyond narrow research and development (R&D) subsidies. Modern innovation policy must embrace the full spectrum of intangible assets – spanning software, data, organizational capital, management capabilities, and brand equity –, while capitalizing on the vital synergies between them. Third, the scalable nature of intangible capital demands a synchronized approach to competition policy, innovation strategy, and corporate finance. Authorities must strike a delicate balance: cultivating the incentives and finance necessary to fuel intangible investments, while simultaneously preventing harmful market concentration and fostering broad diffusion of knowledge.

fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.title: Economists, Economic Knowledge, and Central Banks
fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.author: Juan Acosta
fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.summary: What do economists do in central banks? Why do central banks hire economists? This book investigates the evolving role of economists and economic knowledge within central banks, arguing that their current centrality is neither self-evident nor historically inevitable. While the presence and influence of economists in central banks today may seem natural, this book shows that it is the result of a complex, gradual, and uneven historical process shaped by institutional structures, disciplinary transformations, and shifting relationships between science and policy. Drawing on a rich but dispersed body of literature, the book traces how economists progressively gained authority through the establishment of statistics departments, the adoption of macroeconometric models, and the emergence of a shared cognitive infrastructure between academia and central banks. Rather than focusing on individuals or doctrines, it examines general trends and institutional shifts across a series of national case studies to show how central banks function as boundary organizations, at the intersection of policy and science.

fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.title: Known Unknowns: Knowledge, Confidence, and Public Opinion on Water Reuse
fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.author: Marco Dâ€™Errico
fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.summary: Public acceptance can constrain treated-wastewater reuse, but less is known about whether citizens provide a substantive view at all. An influential account of opposition to contested technologies predicts that the strongest opponents know the least while believing they know the most. We test that joint prediction using a knowledgeâ€“attitudesâ€“practices survey of 1, 069 households in Barbados. The survey separately measures demonstrated topic knowledge, self-assessed knowledge, willingness to use reclaimed water, and explicit 'donâ€™t know' responses. Among respondents who provide a complete willingness profile, demonstrated knowledge is essentially unrelated to acceptance, whereas self-assessed knowledge is positively associated with acceptance. The predicted knowledge-overconfidence configuration therefore does not appear in this setting. The strongest knowledge gradient instead lies on the response margin: a one-standard-deviation increase in demonstrated knowledge is associated with a 5.8-percentage-point lower probability of giving at least one 'donâ€™t know' response, against a base rate of 22.6 per cent. The relationship reappears in three sectoral attitude batteries and attenuates by about 19 per cent after controlling for out-of-module nonresponse. The evidence therefore points away from confidently mistaken opposition and toward a sizeable group that is less knowledgeable and more likely to express uncertainty.

fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.title: Venture Capital and Customer Capital
fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.author: Amir Sufi
fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.summary: Venture capital specializes in the financing of customer capital intensive firms—firms with higher sales and marketing expense to revenue ratios, a higher wage bill for sales and marketing employees, and a higher tendency to apply for trademarks—and they do so more than other financial intermediaries. Venture capitalists target high customer capital industries with low knowledge capital but avoid high knowledge capital industries that lack customer capital. Firms tilt investment toward customer capital leading up to the initial venture capital investment, after which their scale accelerates rapidly. Venture capitalists focus on financing customer capital because such investments require tolerance for substantial risks of failure in pursuit of extreme upside potential, as characterized by power law returns. This return profile fits customer capital investments more closely than investments in knowledge capital. Venture capitalists that sprinkle small investments across a large number of firms, colloquially referred to as the “spray and pray” strategy, target customer capital industries for investment, whereas venture capitalists that commit larger amounts to a small number of firms target knowledge capital industries. The venture capital focus on customer capital reflects a shift away from its traditional focus on knowledge capital intensive firms over the past 30 years.

5b51167fb0:0132a15a91a18b86.title: The Returns to Government R&D: Evidence from US Appropriations Shocks
5b51167fb0:0132a15a91a18b86.author: info@aeaweb.org (Andrew J. Fieldhouse1 and Karel Mertens2 1 Mays Business School, Texas A&M University (email: afieldhouse@mays.tamu.edu) 2 Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, CEPR (email:…
5b51167fb0:0132a15a91a18b86.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 3959-4002 Abstract Based on a narrative classification of all significant postwar changes in R&D appropriations for five major federal agencies, we find that an increase in nondefense R&D appropriations leads to increases in various measures of innovative activity and higher business-sector productivity in the long run. We structurally estimate the production function elasticity of nondefense government R&D capital using the SP-IV methodology of Lewis and Mertens (2024) and obtain implied returns of 140 to 210 percent over the postwar period. The estimates indicate that government-funded R&D accounts for one-fifth of business-sector TFP growth since WWII and imply substantial underfunding of nondefense R&D. (JEL D24, E23, H50, O31, O33, O38)

5b51167fb0:c7fa8e0ff8b591f9.title: The Unequal Economic Consequences of Carbon Pricing
5b51167fb0:c7fa8e0ff8b591f9.author: info@aeaweb.org (Diego R. Känzig1 1 Northwestern University, CEPR, and NBER (email: dkaenzig@northwestern.edu))
5b51167fb0:c7fa8e0ff8b591f9.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4003-4040 Abstract This paper studies the economic impacts of carbon pricing. Exploiting institutional features of the European carbon market and high-frequency data, I identify carbon policy shocks and trace their dynamic effects. A restrictive carbon policy shock raises energy prices, reduces emissions, spurs green innovation, but decreases economic activity—disproportionately burdening poorer households. Not only are the poor more affected because of their higher energy spending, but they also experience larger income losses. These indirect, general equilibrium effects via income and employment play an important role in the transmission of carbon pricing policies, accounting for about two-thirds of the aggregate consumption response. (JEL E23, E24, O44, Q41, Q54, Q55, Q58)

5b51167fb0:e824f86123436e63.title: Residential Segregation and Unequal Access to Local Public Services in India: Evidence from 1.5 Million Neighborhoods
5b51167fb0:e824f86123436e63.author: info@aeaweb.org (Sam Asher1, Kritarth Jha2, Paul Novosad2, Anjali Adukia2 and Brandon Tan3 1 Imperial College London (email: sam.asher@imperial.ac.uk) 2 Development Data Lab (email:…
5b51167fb0:e824f86123436e63.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4041-4076 Abstract We study residential segregation and access to public services across 1.5 million urban and rural neighborhoods in India. Muslim and Scheduled Caste segregation in India is high by global standards and only slightly lower than Black-White segregation in the United States. Within cities, public facilities and infrastructure are systematically less available in Muslim and Scheduled Caste neighborhoods. Nearly all regressive allocation is across neighborhoods within cities—at the most informal and least studied form of government. These inequalities are not visible in the aggregate data typically used for research and policy. (JEL H76, J15, O15, O17, O18, R23)

5b51167fb0:ed6f6ae7997930cd.title: Durables and the Marginal Propensity to Spend
5b51167fb0:ed6f6ae7997930cd.author: info@aeaweb.org (Nathan Zorzi1 and Martin Beraja2 1 Dartmouth (email: Nathan.G.Zorzi@dartmouth.edu) 2 UC Berkeley and NBER (email: maberaja@berkeley.edu))
5b51167fb0:ed6f6ae7997930cd.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4077-4115 Abstract Durables represent a large share of households' marginal propensity to spend (MPX). We develop a quantitative model of spending that takes durables into account and matches a rich set of empirical regularities simultaneously. Scaling the response of nondurables provides a poor approximation of the MPX on durables when it comes to its distribution in the population, its persistence over time, and its cyclicality. As an application, we study how the MPX varies with the size of stimulus checks and find that it declines more slowly compared to a model of purely nondurable spending. (JEL D11, E21, E32, E62, G51)

5b51167fb0:3196e21e18145698.title: Union Bargaining Power and the Amenity-Wage Trade-Off
5b51167fb0:3196e21e18145698.author: info@aeaweb.org (Lorenzo Lagos1 1 Brown University, NBER, and IZA (email: lorenzo_lagos@brown.edu))
5b51167fb0:3196e21e18145698.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4116-4157 Abstract This paper studies how collective bargaining affects wages and amenities. By merging collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) to linked employer-employee data in Brazil, I combine rich contracted amenities with wage information. I implement a difference-in-differences strategy that exploits a court ruling enforcing CBA continuation (i.e., ultra-activity) to estimate the effects of union bargaining power. Strengthening unions raises wages and amenities without reducing employment—increasing retention despite some labor-labor substitution. A revealed-preference approach shows that amenities account for 45 percent of total compensation gains. These findings suggest that collective bargaining can offset monopsony power, but employers retain the right-to-manage workforce composition. (JEL J31, J32, J42, J51, J52, O15)

5b51167fb0:040a01a62b7769bc.title: Inequality and Racial Backlash: Evidence from the Reconstruction Era and the Freedmen's Bureau
5b51167fb0:040a01a62b7769bc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Eric Chyn1, Kareem Haggag2 and Bryan A. Stuart3 1 Department of Economics, University of Texas-Austin, and NBER (email: eric.chyn@austin.utexas.edu) 2 Anderson School of Management,…
5b51167fb0:040a01a62b7769bc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4158-4202 Abstract How do majority groups respond to narrowing inequality in racially polarized environments? We study this by examining the Freedmen's Bureau, an agency created after the US Civil War to aid former slaves and launch institutional reform in the South. Using new historical records and an event-study approach, we estimate the bureau's impact on political, social, and economic outcomes. Vote shares for Democrats, the party that previously championed slavery and opposed Black civil rights, initially eroded in bureau counties, but these impacts faded as federal oversight weakened. Racial backlash emerged rapidly and persisted, suggesting White majorities sought to offset Black progress. (JEL D63, D72, J15, N31, N41)

5b51167fb0:0ad09d14a2108386.title: The Inflation Attention Threshold and Inflation Surges
5b51167fb0:0ad09d14a2108386.author: info@aeaweb.org (Oliver Pfäuti1 1 The University of Texas at Austin (email: pfaeuti.oliver@gmail.com))
5b51167fb0:0ad09d14a2108386.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4203-4242 Abstract The recent inflation surge brought inflation back on people's minds. I quantify when and how much attention to inflation changes and derive the macroeconomic implications of these attention changes. I estimate an attention threshold at an inflation rate of 4 percent, that attention doubles when inflation exceeds this threshold, and that supply shocks have stronger and more persistent effects on inflation in times of high attention. Developing a model featuring the attention threshold, I show that attention changes offer a joint explanation for inflation surges, inflation's co-movement with inflation expectations, and a long last mile of disinflation. (JEL D84, E12, E31, E43, E52)

5b51167fb0:cde519eb240cea67.title: The Causal Effects of Global Supply Chain Disruptions on Macroeconomic Outcomes: Evidence and Theory
5b51167fb0:cde519eb240cea67.author: info@aeaweb.org (Xiwen Bai1, Jesús Fernández-Villaverde2, Yiliang Li3 and Francesco Zanetti4 1 Tsinghua University (email: xiwenbai@mail.tsinghua.edu.cn) 2 University of Pennsylvania (email:…
5b51167fb0:cde519eb240cea67.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4243-4281 Abstract We study the causal effects of global supply chain disruptions by constructing a new index of real-time port congestion using Automatic Identification System data from container ships and a spatial clustering algorithm. We develop a model with search frictions between producers and retailers that links upstream production slack to downstream supply shortages and captures output and price responses to supply chain shocks. The co-movements of output, prices, spare capacity, and market tightness provide novel identification restrictions. We find that demand and supply shocks drove US disinflation in 2020, while the inflation surge in 2021 was driven mainly by supply chain shocks. (JEL C43, E31, F14, F23, L14, L92)

5b51167fb0:e1d96c9b68fa4eb6.title: Firm Adaptation in Production Networks: Evidence from Extreme Weather Events in Pakistan
5b51167fb0:e1d96c9b68fa4eb6.author: info@aeaweb.org (Clare Balboni1, Johannes Boehm2 and Mazhar Waseem 1 London School of Economics and Political Science (email: c.a.balboni@lse.ac.uk) 2 University of Geneva (email:…
5b51167fb0:e1d96c9b68fa4eb6.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4282-4325 Abstract This paper considers how far private adaptation may reduce future vulnerability to climate risks. Using data on monthly firm-to-firm transactions from Pakistan, we find that flood-affected firms are more likely to relocate to safer ground and shift purchases toward suppliers in less flood-prone regions and reached via less flood-prone roads. The results indicate that firms are imperfectly informed about flood risk and update their beliefs following floods. We quantify aggregate impacts using a spatial model of endogenous production network formation. The findings suggest that firms' learning will shape the economic impact of increasingly frequent climate-related disasters. (JEL D22, L14, O13, O14, Q54, R32)

5b51167fb0:f3cbadd0645f288a.title: Reproducible Aggregation of Sample-Split Statistics
5b51167fb0:f3cbadd0645f288a.author: info@aeaweb.org (David M. Ritzwoller1 and Joseph P. Romano2 1 Stanford University (email: ritzwoll@stanford.edu) 2 Stanford University (email: romano@stanford.edu))
5b51167fb0:f3cbadd0645f288a.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4326-4357 Abstract Statistical inference is often simplified by sample splitting. This simplification comes at the cost of the introduction of randomness not native to the data. We propose a simple procedure for sequentially aggregating statistics constructed with multiple splits of the same sample. The user specifies a bound and a nominal error rate. If the procedure is implemented twice on the same data, the nominal error rate approximates the chance that the results differ by more than the bound. We illustrate the application of the procedure to several widely applied econometric methods. (JEL C20, C30, C52)

21113a7a19:ceb8f0e6118ab179.title: Jlateh Vincent Jappah, on the job market--a remarkable candidate
21113a7a19:ceb8f0e6118ab179.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:ceb8f0e6118ab179.summary: Not for the first time, I have a remarkable student on the job market this year, Jlateh Vincent Jappah . Born in Liberia and now a US citizen, Vincent is on an unusual intellectual and academic journey. He is presently finishing his PhD in Health Policy here at Stanford, and has also taken a full load of graduate courses in the Economics department. He is also a physician, with an MD from a Russian medical school. I am co-supervising his dissertation with my colleague Caroline Hoxby. His main project is on the impact of incentives on blood donation in Sub-Saharan Africa. His results are dramatic. Per-diem cash payments, e.g. for transportation, are far more effective and much less expensive than telephone credits or meals for eliciting safe blood donation. If he sounds really special, it's because he is. I'll be happy to correspond with anyone interested in pursuing him on this year's job market.

21113a7a19:2ee7f4f10d726586.title: Human organ trafficking and missing persons in China, PNAS
21113a7a19:2ee7f4f10d726586.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:2ee7f4f10d726586.summary: Here's a study, recently published in PNAS, that tries to very indirectly infer the rate of illegal organ trafficking in China. It's sure to be controversial. X. Wang, Human organ trafficking and missing persons in China , Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 123 (44) e2608464123, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2608464123 (2026). "Abstract The persistent shortage of human organs for transplantation has long been a global challenge. The prospect of substantial profit creates strong incentives for illegal organ trafficking, including murder for organ harvesting, yet empirical evidence remains scarce. This study addresses this gap by exploiting a unique quasi-natural experiment created by China’s organ policy reform. From 1984 to 2014, executed prisoners were the primary source of transplant organs in China. In 2015, the Chinese government abolished the use of organs from executed prisoners, sharply exacerbating the organ shortage. Following this policy change, the number of missing persons rose notably nationwide. Employing difference-in-differences and triple-difference strategies, we show that, compared to cases unrelated to organ trafficking (e.g., voluntary disappearances), the number and incidence of involuntary missing persons plausibly related to organ trafficking increased significantly after 2015. The effects are especially pronounced among individuals with mental illness and in regions with higher transplant demand and greater transplant capacity. Although we do not directly observe organ trafficking, the spatial, temporal, and demographic patterns we document are consistent with the hypothesis that increased organ scarcity intensified incentives for illicit organ procurement. More broadly, the findings suggest that severe organ shortages may generate unintended and highly harmful consequences, even in a low-crime setting such as China. These results underscore the importance of accounting for behavioral responses and illicit-market incentives when designing…

Below are the PNAS paper, the SFUSD announcements, and then some links to the history of school choice in SF. I. Lo, K. Mentzer, M. YahyazadehJeloudar, H. O’Connell, J. Monardo, & I. November 2, 2026, e2524796123, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2524796123 (2026). "Abstract. More than 65 years after the Brown v. Board of Education ruling that school segregation is unconstitutional, public schools across the United States are again experiencing rising segregation. In districts like San Francisco, efforts to implement district-wide choice policies have largely failed to reverse these trends. Since 2019, we have collaborated with the San Francisco Unified School District to design a student assignment policy meeting the district’s goals of diversity, predictability, and proximity. 21113a7a19:64876eeda3cb87cc.summary: I returned from a long trip and an arduous conference last week to learn that two important economists had passed away, Bill Nordhaus, who won a Nobel, and Jim Andreoni, who could have. Nordhaus' work on climate change was prescient, and is well known. Here's the Nordhaus obit from Yale: William Nordhaus, Nobel laureate who integrated economics and climate change, devoted Yale citizen Oct 31, 2026 By Penelope Laurans "William Nordhaus ‘63, Sterling Professor of Economics who won a Nobel Prize in 2018 for integrating climate change into long-run macroeconomic analysis, died Oct. 30 at age 85. ########## Jim Andreoni was a multi-talented scholar of public goods, well known in the experimental economics community. The work that in my mind made him a Nobel candidate was his work on different forms that altruism can take. Two of his papers that I really like are Andreoni, James. "Impure altruism and donations to public goods: A theory of warm-glow giving." The economic journal 100, no. 401 (1990): 464-477. and James Andreoni, Justin M. Rao, and Hannah Trachtman, Avoiding the Ask: A Field Experiment on Altruism, Empathy, and Charitable Giving. Journal of Political Economy 2017 125:625-653. The first of those, a theory paper, I think of as one of the foundational papers about effective altruism, but from the point of view that much altruism is not primarily of the effective sort. The second paper is an experiment that I'll present to my class today, in Jim's memory. ############# Vigorous, personal disagreement about what constitutes altruism in organ donation and transplantation was what made my Geneva conference so arduous (and what makes the kinds of controversial markets I discuss in Moral Economics so controversial:). 21113a7a19:ee0ff3f10b82afff.title: Sports, ethnicity, and the urban geography of basketball
21113a7a19:ee0ff3f10b82afff.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:ee0ff3f10b82afff.summary: I'm just back from an unexpectedly grueling trip, and hope to resume semi-daily blogging. This story caught my eye: basketball has been an inner city game in the U.S., in part because basketball courts can be set up very inexpensively in urban parks, and not so expensively in gyms. So inner city kids are disproportionately represented among the most talented players. But who those kids are has changed over time. The WSJ has the story: When Jews Ruled the Basketball Court. Six players on the New York Knicks’ inaugural roster were Jewish. By Michael Freund "It was Nov. 1, 1946, and Ossie Schectman of the New York Knicks took a bounce pass and scored on a two-handed underhand layup. Schectman, the son of Russian Jewish immigrants, had just scored the first basket in NBA history. ... "Six members of the Knicks’ original roster, including Schectman, were Jewish. That was no coincidence. For much of the early 20th century, basketball was widely regarded as a Jewish game. "The reason can be traced to the immigrant neighborhoods of New York and Philadelphia. Millions of Jews arrived from Eastern Europe beginning in the 1880s, often settling in neighborhoods with little open space and scant money to spend on recreation. Baseball required a field and equipment. Basketball needed little more than a ball, a hoop and a schoolyard. "

CHI DECIDE? VITA, LIBERTÀ E CONFINI MORALI WHO GETS TO CHOOSE? LIFE, FREEDOM, AND MORAL BOUNDARIES sabato 24 ottobre 17:00 - 18:00 Centro Città Collegio Carlo Alberto | Auditorium Piazza Vincenzo Arbarello, 8, Torino With MARCO CAPPATO, ALVIN ROTH Moderates CATERINA SOFFICI Live translation available Quando le scelte riguardano il corpo, la vita e la morte, dove finisce la libertà individuale e dove deve iniziare la regolazione pubblica? Cosa dovrebbero fare le società quando le convinzioni morali divergono profondamente? Come possono le istituzioni proteggere la libertà di scelta senza lasciare indifesi i più vulnerabili? When choices involve the body, life, and death, where should individual freedom end and public regulation begin? What should societies do when moral convictions sharply diverge? How can institutions protect freedom of choice without leaving the most vulnerable unprotected?

21113a7a19:4a1e5a37dfce9f4e.title: Market design and water conservation in the the Great Salt Lake
21113a7a19:4a1e5a37dfce9f4e.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:4a1e5a37dfce9f4e.summary: Silvia Console Battilana, who co-founded Auctionomics along with Paul Milgrom, writes in Forbes about the prospects for market design efforts to help conserve Utah's Great Salt Lake. How Market Design Could Help Save Utah’s Great Salt Lake by By Silvia Console Battilana "the Great Salt Lake is drying up. "To save the lake while protecting water users, business leaders can adopt a little-known but powerful economic tool: market design. When water levels drop, the consequences immediately hit commercial supply chains and local commerce. Market-based incentives give businesses a way to reward upstream water conservation, bringing more water to the lake without hurting regional growth. The invisible hand of the market could identify the least expensive conservation, compensate participating water users and restore the Great Salt Lake. ... "The shrinking of the Great Salt Lake has many causes, and there is no silver-bullet fix. But any solution to refill the lake will likely involve conservation within Utah. Seventy-one percent of the water diverted from the lake’s basin is allocated to agriculture. If those commercial users could make more efficient use of water, more would reach the lake. The catch is that many conservation practices, like water-friendly infrastructure and precision irrigation, are expensive. Under Utah’s traditional “use-it-or-lose-it” water rights system, users have little financial reason to conserve. Without modern economic incentives, asking businesses and farms to voluntarily cut back simply isn’t realistic. Even if water users could be forced to cut back, it’s not clear who should cut back, or by how much. The costs of water conservation aren’t the same across users, and they can be very hard to estimate. Market design can address both of these challenges. Crucially, markets don’t force particular actions or behaviors. Instead, well-designed markets create an incentive for farms and communities to cut back on water and be rewarded for their…

21113a7a19:093967ed777c5557.title: Moral Economics reviewed in American Journal of Transplantation
21113a7a19:093967ed777c5557.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:093967ed777c5557.summary: I wonder if this is the first time an economics book has been reviewed in the American Journal of Transplantation. Poetic justice: A review of moral economics by Alvin E. Roth Michael A. Rees "Alvin E. Roth describes poetic justice as the Virginia state flag flying at half-mast in 2020 in honor of Bernie Cohen, who argued the US Supreme Court case Loving v. Virginia that made interracial marriage legal. Turns out Mildred and Richard Loving were convicted of interracial marriage in 1967, arrested by police at 2 AM at home in their bed, and sentenced to 1 year in prison but suspended on the condition that they leave Virginia for 25 years. Reading what the Virginia Court of Appeals judge wrote, side by side with what the US Supreme Court wrote, is, by itself, worth the price of the book. "Those of us in the field of transplantation have felt—and will continue to feel—the impact of repugnance. In moral economics, Alvin E. Roth takes us on a grand tour of how repugnance shapes transactions across a wide spectrum of human activities. Take uterus transplantation, pioneered in Sweden, a country where repugnance to surrogacy has made it illegal. You can transplant a uterus into a woman with infertility in Sweden, but do not you dare use a surrogate’s uterus in her own body to help you achieve a baby! Alvin E. Roth defines repugnance as a morally contested market that some people would like to participate in, but others think should be outlawed. He goes on to call a transaction repugnant if “all parties to the transaction want to engage in it, and others think they shouldn’t be allowed to for moral or religious reasons, even though those others can’t detect that the transaction has taken place unless someone tells them.”1 I found it fascinating to walk through all the ways in which repugnance has shaped the world in which we live. "The book starts with a clear example of a transaction that many people want to engage in: sex. Of course, I knew about the repugnance…

21113a7a19:2fce76346ec91464.title: Kidney exchange may (re)emerge in Korea
21113a7a19:2fce76346ec91464.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:2fce76346ec91464.summary: Kidney exchange, which was pioneered in South Korea in the late 1990's, has largely been moribund there. But here's a call to change that. Reemerging kidney paired donation in Korea: simultaneous two-way swaps to overcome human leukocyte antigen and anatomic barriers Eunjeong Kang1,2, Kyung Ok Min1, Hee Gyung Kang3, Yohan Ahn3, Eun Young Song4, Ara Cho5, Ahram Han5, Sangil Min5, Jongwon Ha5,6,7, Sehoon Park2, Yong Chul Kim2, Yon Su Kim2,8, Hajeong Lee2,8 Kidney Research and Clinical Practice 2026;j.krcp.25.391. DOI: https://doi.org/10.23876/j.krcp.25.391 Abstract Background South Korea first implemented kidney paired donation (KPD) to overcome ABO-incompatible living-donor kidney transplantation. Although utilization declined as desensitization matured, persistent desensitization failure and anatomic constraints have renewed interest in KPD within a regulated framework. We report a recent single-center experience. Methods KPD exchanges were coordinated within an institutional registry under national supervision. We retrospectively reviewed six consecutive, simultaneous two-way exchanges (12 recipients) from 2022 to 2025. We assessed predefined desensitization failure or anticipated failure with the intended donor, compared immunologic compatibility between intended and exchange donors, and recorded perioperative desensitization, graft function, delayed graft function (DGF), and biopsy-proven acute rejection (BPAR). Results Five of six exchanges were undertaken for immunologic reasons. All five met criteria for desensitization failure or anticipated failure to the intended donor, with positive crossmatch and high donor-specific antibody (DSA) burden. Reassignment to the exchange donor reduced risk, lowering maximum DSA mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) from 13,228 to 1,350 and total DSA MFI from 20,542 to 2,240, although selective desensitization was still required in some recipients with residual human leukocyte antigen or ABO incompatibility. 21113a7a19:76ed32eea3176b4f.summary: There are two ways of measuring the success of military measures to limit the supply of cocaine. There's the military measure of how many people are killed and how much cocaine is confiscated. And there's the economic measure of how much cocaine is available to consumers, at what price and quality. The WSJ has the story (of plunging prices and rising quality): Why U.S. Airstrikes Are Failing to Stop the Global Cocaine Boom Smugglers are shifting routes and using new tactics to evade military targeting, resulting in record supplies, plunging prices and high purity in the U.S. and Europe by Juan Forero | "BUENAVENTURA, Colombia—The Trump administration’s bombing campaign against cocaine-smuggling speedboats is starting to have an impact on the global drug trade—but not necessarily in a good way. ... " Record supplies of cocaine still arrive in the U.S., Europe and as far away as Australia every day, cheaper and purer than they’ve been in decades , said law-enforcement officials across four continents. " President Trump has celebrated the airstrikes, noting his administration has “made tremendous strides in stopping the flow of illegal drugs into our country.” In the past 13 months, American military drones and aircraft have destroyed more than 70 vessels, killing nearly 240 crew members and depriving criminal groups of $1.5 billion in cocaine, according to U.S. officials. “The drugs coming in by sea are down by 97%,” Trump said in June. “We’re trying to figure out who the 3% are, because they are the bravest people on earth.” ... In Miami, wholesale cocaine sold for about $16,500 a kilogram this summer, well below the historical $22,000 to $25,000 range.
