21113a7a19:0b3e864f26759c4c.title: Kidney exchange in India at a national scale: a growing consensus
21113a7a19:0b3e864f26759c4c.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:0b3e864f26759c4c.summary: There's growing consensus in India on moving towards a nationwide kidney exchange program. Kute V, Kumar A, Balwani M et al. Operational guidelines for kidney swap transplantation in India: an ISOT-NOTTO Delphi consensus The Lancet Regional Health – Southeast Asia, 2026; 0 Among the consensus recommendations is this one, which summarizes the general positive tone adopted for national kidney exchange. "Each transplant center should initiate and expand swap transplantation, given that it is legal, cost-effective, yields better outcomes, and can help prevent unethical commercial transplants by improving access. Multicentric swap transplantation programmes should roll out in phases: start with intra-city exchanges, then intra-state, and eventually inter-state and national collaborations. This phased approach ensures growing scale is matched with operational readiness, providing safe, equitable, and efficient transplants across regions."

21113a7a19:c6f9ebdacc9b1381.title: The University of Cincinnati celebrates Steve Woodle
21113a7a19:c6f9ebdacc9b1381.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:c6f9ebdacc9b1381.summary: Dr. Steve Woodle, one of the pioneers of kidney exchange, is being honored in Cincinnati. You can read of his many distinctions below, but here's a striking one: he is the " the first liver transplant recipient to perform a liver transplant ." 2026 Daniel Drake Medals The University of Cincinnati College of Medicine’s highest honor E. Steve Woodle, MD E. Steve Woodle, MD Woodle, professor of surgery and the William A. Altemeier endowed chair in surgery at the College of Medicine, is a multiorgan transplant surgeon and transplant immunologist who has spent more than four decades advancing the understanding of organ rejection and pioneering immunosuppressive therapies that have reshaped transplantation. Earlier in his career at the University of Chicago, he performed a liver transplant on a 10-day-old infant, setting a Guinness World Record for the youngest liver transplant recipient. He joined the College of Medicine in 1999 and directed the Division of Transplantation for nearly two decades, building an internationally recognized program of clinical and research excellence. In 2001, he performed Ohio’s first allogeneic islet transplant for type 1 diabetes. After undergoing his own liver transplant in 2003, Woodle returned to the operating room and became the first liver transplant recipient to perform a liver transplant. Woodle has helped originate several therapeutic approaches now considered standard in transplantation. As a fellow, he conceived the genetic re-engineering of OKT3, the first FDA-approved monoclonal antibody — work later developed into teplizumab (Tzield), which the FDA approved in 2022 as the first immunomodulatory therapy for type 1 diabetes. He was the first investigator to introduce plasma cell-targeted therapy for a non-malignant human disease, using proteasome inhibitors to treat antibody-mediated rejection in kidney transplant recipients. 2f5fdda6a0:5040f704210b6386.title: Measuring the Cost of Regulation: A Text-Based Approach
2f5fdda6a0:5040f704210b6386.author: Yang, Ruoke
2f5fdda6a0:5040f704210b6386.summary: We derive a measure of firm-level regulatory exposure from corporate earnings calls text and study its effects on growth, leverage, profitability, and equity returns. Higher regulatory exposure results in slower sales and asset growth, lower leverage, reduced profitability, and higher post-call equity returns. Most of these effects are mitigated for larger firms. We validate our measure by showing its explanatory power for cross-sectional stock returns during the 2016 Presidential election.

2f5fdda6a0:7e61b2d867f170d8.title: Do Banks Overreact to Disaster Risk?
2f5fdda6a0:7e61b2d867f170d8.author: Yuan, Tao
2f5fdda6a0:7e61b2d867f170d8.summary: We examine how banks respond to natural disasters when borrowers are in proximity to affected areas. We find robust evidence that banks impose significantly higher loan spreads on firms in these areas following a disaster compared to other borrowers. This effect diminishes over time and is stronger for loans with concentrated syndicates, disasters with greater media coverage, and cases in which loan officers are geographically closer to disaster sites. The increased financing costs result in capital constraints for affected firms. Overall, our findings highlight a salience bias in banks’ evaluation of borrowers’ disaster risk, with adverse effects on borrowing firms.

2f5fdda6a0:0ab1df10e85b4341.title: Appointing Charity Directors in Response to ESG Incidents
2f5fdda6a0:0ab1df10e85b4341.author: Zhang, Yuyang
2f5fdda6a0:0ab1df10e85b4341.summary: This article examines how companies respond to negative ESG incidents by appointing directors with charitable organization experience. Firms are more likely to make these appointments following high-profile ESG incidents, especially those involving social issues. The market reacts positively, particularly when directors’ biographies emphasize their charity experience. Using the local supply of charity directors as an instrumental variable, we show that incidents, particularly workforce-related incidents, decline after these appointments, with effects driven by nonoverboarded directors. Overall, our study documents a value-enhancing human capital channel through which firms address ESG concerns.

2f5fdda6a0:56ed393d7aa87044.title: Get the Money Somehow: The Effect of Missing Performance Goals on Insider Trading
2f5fdda6a0:56ed393d7aa87044.author: Gao, Meng
2f5fdda6a0:56ed393d7aa87044.summary: This article uses a regression discontinuity design to identify the effect of compensation shocks on insider trading. I find that CEOs who narrowly miss relative performance goals and hence suffer a loss in compensation subsequently earn higher abnormal profits from their insider trades than otherwise similar CEOs who narrowly beat such goals. CEOs who narrowly miss relative performance goals also become less likely to provide earnings and sales guidance. These results suggest that managers can use insider trading to make up for compensation losses due to missing relative performance goals, which could reduce the incentive effect of performance-based pay.

a8e07c2372:e305db06d016b78f.title: The Care and Feeding of a European AI Unicorn

04be1a0d28:b30048d963e83690.title: Designing Low Emission Zones: Theory and Evidence -- by Nano Barahona, Natalia Fabra, Imelda, Juan-Pablo Montero
04be1a0d28:b30048d963e83690.summary: Low Emission Zones (LEZs), which exclude polluting vehicles from parts of a city, are spreading. Yet how their design affects welfare is poorly understood. Unlike price instruments, LEZs ration access inefficiently, imposing costs on inframarginal drivers of restricted vehicles. In our model, welfare is quasi-convex in LEZ size, yielding bang-bang principles: LEZs should be as large as possible or not implemented at all; cleaner vehicles (e.g., hybrids) could be exempt as transition technologies but later restricted, which may require planner commitment. Using new-car purchases, we find Madrid’s LEZ shifted buyers toward cleaner cars, but the surplus losses of switchers and inframarginal drivers exceeded emission savings.

04be1a0d28:86de3caf15beb00a.title: Five Facts About Stablecoins -- by Lin William Cong, Gordon Y. Liao, Eswar S. Prasad, Tony Zhang
04be1a0d28:86de3caf15beb00a.summary: We document five facts about payment stablecoins using wallet-level blockchain data from 2020 to 2025. First, stablecoins serve as a transaction currency: onchain volume exceeds Bitcoin’s despite a much smaller supply, velocity has risen sharply, and transactions have shifted toward low-value transfers. Second, using transaction timing to refine exchange-based attribution, we find activity spread across the Americas, Europe, and Asia and fewer cross-regional flows than the standard method implies. Third, we estimate a structural cash-management model on the holdings data and find that the costs of accessing stablecoin wallets have fallen since 2023. Fourth, stablecoins are becoming the settlement currency of a fast-growing onchain credit market, and their growth appears to reallocate rather than destroy credit. Fifth, smart contracts are involved in about a third of Ethereum stablecoin transactions and over two thirds of volume, and protocols such as x402 demonstrate sub-cent machine-to-machine payments. Stablecoins behave as tokenized money, with implications for financial markets and regulation.
