f965d2251a:62a3a5dec33f1007.title: Retrieval Failures and Consumption Smoothing: A Field Experiment on Seasonal Poverty*
f965d2251a:62a3a5dec33f1007.summary: Abstract People may fail to recall and use information they already know when making decisions. We empirically investigate whether such “retrieval failures” distort consumption-smoothing behavior among Zambian farmers, who derive their income from one annual harvest and spend it over the course of the year. We document that individuals underestimate upcoming spending by 50%, creating scope for undersaving. To improve recall, we randomize an intervention that prompts people to think through their future expenses associatively in categories—without providing any external information or guidance. Treated individuals increase “remembered” expenses by 36%–60%; as predicted by the memory literature, effects are concentrated among small, irregular, and stochastic items. Immediate spending drops and, six weeks after the intervention, treated households hold 15% higher savings. They subsequently enter the hungry season—the final months of the year when consumption typically declines sharply—with one additional month of savings, leading to a flatter spending profile over the year. Households use the increased savings to self-finance additional farm investment, resulting in a 9% increase in the next year’s crop revenue. We replicate the intervention’s effect on beliefs among low-income Americans, suggesting that retrieval failures generalize across settings and populations.

f965d2251a:c79bdfba8535da03.title: Busing to Opportunity? The Impacts of the Metco Voluntary School Desegregation Program on Urban Students of Color
f965d2251a:c79bdfba8535da03.summary: Abstract School assignment policies are a key lever for expanding access to high-performing schools and promoting racial and socioeconomic integration. For over 50 years, the Metropolitan Council for Educational Opportunity (METCO) has bussed students of color from Boston, Massachusetts, to relatively wealthier and predominantly white suburbs. I estimate the effects of attending a high-performing suburban school by comparing applicants who receive enrollment offers with applicants who do not. A two-stage least squares approach exploits waitlist assignment priorities and controls for a rich set of characteristics from birth records and application data. Attending a suburban school boosts math and English test scores, reduces dropout, and increases on-time high school graduation. Four-year college aspirations, enrollment, and graduation increase along with earnings in adulthood. Students whose parents did not attend college and boys experience the largest effects. The evidence points to several mechanisms, including access to higher value-added schools, higher-achieving peers, and schools with stronger college-going norms. Participants are more likely to be tracked into lower-performing classes, implying that effects could be larger with access to more advanced coursework. District value-added estimates suggest that students’ educational trajectories shift at least as much as they would from growing up in the suburban districts.

f965d2251a:7e3356847366fb7c.title: Bringing Work Home: Flexible Work Arrangements as Gateway Jobs for Women in West Bengal*
f965d2251a:7e3356847366fb7c.summary: Abstract There is a large latent workforce in developing countries that consists of hundreds of millions of women who prefer to have paid work and yet are out of the labor force. Often, available job opportunities are incompatible with traditional gender roles that encourage women to stay at home. In a randomized experiment with 1,670 households, we partner with a jobs platform to offer short-term data work to women who are out of the labor force. We find three main results. First, flexible work-from-home jobs are highly effective at bringing women into paid work. Job flexibility more than triples take-up from 15% for an office job to 48% for a job that women can do from home while multitasking with childcare. Second, these jobs can act as a stepping stone to less flexible work. Trying paid work from home increases take-up of less flexible jobs two to three months later among women without previous work experience. “Gateway jobs” are especially important for women from more traditional households: their labor supply is more likely to be marginal to flexibility, and in turn, work experience shifts their attitudes to become less traditional. Third, from the labor demand side, remote work comes with trade-offs in worker performance. Working from the office increases accuracy by 3% and speed by 18%. However, these performance drawbacks of work-from-home arrangements may be outweighed by the increase in available workers.

f965d2251a:e4c5cce8c2a59ace.title: Fairness Across the World
f965d2251a:e4c5cce8c2a59ace.summary: Abstract This article provides the first comprehensive global evidence on people’s fairness and efficiency preferences, beliefs about the sources of inequality and the efficiency cost of redistribution, and policy attitudes toward redistribution. Using a globally harmonized consequential experiment with more than 65,000 individuals across 60 countries, we show that the source of inequality plays a substantially larger role for inequality acceptance than the efficiency cost of redistribution. At the global level, implemented inequality increases by 85% when inequality is caused by merit rather than luck, compared with a 14% increase when redistribution entails a 50% efficiency cost. We document substantial heterogeneity in fairness views and beliefs within and across societies. The meritocratic fairness view is most prominent in many richer Western societies, while libertarian and egalitarian fairness views are widespread in many other parts of the world. Globally, people are more likely to believe that inequality reflects luck rather than merit, while beliefs in large efficiency costs of redistribution are relatively weak. Fairness preferences and beliefs are strongly associated with redistribution attitudes and actual redistribution through taxes and transfers across countries. Our findings illustrate how the interaction between fairness views and beliefs may shape redistribution across societies, highlighting the importance of jointly understanding preferences and beliefs in the political economy of redistribution.

f965d2251a:c5028e4bcde9f322.title: Wealth and Property Taxation in the United States*
f965d2251a:c5028e4bcde9f322.summary: Abstract We study the history and geography of wealth accumulation in the United States using newly collected historical property tax records from the early 1800s onward. These records come from the administration of the General Property Tax—a tax that aspired to cover all types of property. We construct wealth series at the state, county, and national levels. At the state level, we use annual assessed values of wealth from state-level reports drawn from multiple sources. Because assessed values may differ from market values, we also require assessment ratios, defined as the ratio of assessed to market wealth. We obtain state-level assessment ratios from decadal U.S. Census wealth data (drawn from various census reports, including those on “Wealth, Debt, and Taxation”), in which the census carried out detailed valuation work, complemented with information on changes in assessment practices from the state reports, to build higher-frequency series of assessment ratios. The result is long-run annual wealth series for states from 1850 (or earlier, depending on the state) to 1935. We obtain national wealth series by aggregating these state series. At the county level, we use assessed values (or market values where available) from the U.S. Census wealth data for each decade and apply either state-level or county-level assessment ratios, where available, to obtain market values of wealth for each decade from 1850 to 1930. We use these data to show, first, that the United States experienced extraordinary wealth accumulation after the Civil War and until the Great Depression. Second, spatial inequality in the United States has been large and highly persistent since the mid-1800s. We also examine the determinants of long-term wealth growth and find, among other results, that counties with a higher share of enslaved property before the Civil War or with higher wealth inequality experienced lower subsequent long-run wealth growth.

56c7f0b50e:cdc137d4cf8df976.title: The Long-Term Mental Health Consequences of Emotional and Interpersonal Work Demands
56c7f0b50e:cdc137d4cf8df976.author: Vincent Vandenberghe
56c7f0b50e:cdc137d4cf8df976.summary: This paper examines how career-long emotional/interpersonal work demands are associated with mental health among adults aged 50 and older. Using retrospective work histories from SHARE combined with ISCO-4-level occupational characteristics from O*NET, we construct employment trajectories capturing cumulative exposure to emotionally/interpersonally demanding work and examine its association with later-life depressive symptoms, measured by the EURO-D scale. Our findings show that careerlong emotional/interpersonal demands are associated with a higher risk of depression after age 50, although their relative importance is modest. Career instability, such as employment gaps, redundancies, and part-time work, emerges as a stronger predictor. Pre-labour-market factors, including childhood health and educational attainment, also play a substantial role, highlighting the lasting importance of early-life circumstances for later-life mental health.

56c7f0b50e:c4569102b5bc0242.title: The Geography of Job Search, Social Networks and Match Quality
56c7f0b50e:c4569102b5bc0242.author: Zaharieva, Anna
56c7f0b50e:c4569102b5bc0242.summary: We study a relationship between the job search strategies of workers and occupational mismatch, and investigate the role of worker mobility. Using data from the German Socio-economic Panel, we show that workers finding jobs through social contacts experience shorter moving distances compared to workers finding jobs formally. However, shorter moving distances are associated with higher occupational mismatch. Building on this geography-based mechanism, we develop a theoretical search and matching model where individuals are uniformly distributed on a unit distance between two cities and seek a job in either city by applying formally or using help of their network contacts. Jobs have heterogeneous match qualities and there is a moving cost. Beyond explaining the evidence, the model predicts that network hiring leads to a stronger concentration of workers in the cities and contributes to the regional employment segregation. Moreover, it raises inequality by widening the gap in life-time incomes across locations.

56c7f0b50e:9084ec65e34eef4d.title: The Division of Labor: Productivity, Coordination, and Learning
56c7f0b50e:9084ec65e34eef4d.author: Xu, Yaling
56c7f0b50e:9084ec65e34eef4d.summary: The division of labor is fundamental to how firms organize production. Since Adam Smith, economists have recognized that dividing tasks more finely increases productivity through specialization but also raises coordination costs—a tradeoff formalized by Becker and Murphy (1992). Yet we have little systematic evidence on how this tradeoff operates within firms. Moreover, this classical perspective overlooks a second, dynamic tradeoff: firms not only produce output, but also develop a central input into future production—their workers’ human capital. A finer division of labor allows workers to develop greater expertise through repeated performance of narrowly defined tasks, but may also reduce opportunities to learn from coworkers by limiting interactions and knowledge exchange. We study both tradeoffs using population-wide Norwegian employer–employee records, linked workplace surveys, quasi-experimental variation in coworker availability, and randomized experiments with workers and managers. We find that more specialized firms exhibit higher productivity but also greater coordination costs. Their workers report more learning-by-doing but substantially less coworker learning, resulting in lower overall learning and slower wage growth. To establish the importance of coworker learning for human capital accumulation, we exploit extended coworker absences and show that losing access to colleagues reduces subsequent wage growth, particularly in occupations characterized by greater task overlap and coworker learning. To isolate the role of the division of labor from other workplace characteristics, we conduct randomized experiments that vary task allocation in otherwise identical workplaces. Workers and managers anticipate greater coordination demands, weaker coworker interactions, and lower skill accumulation under greater specialization. The experiments then ask workers to choose their preferred workplace and managers how they would organize production. Both favor…

56c7f0b50e:43b515f4c0da2167.title: What is an AI worker? Evidence from Matched Vacancy-Hires
56c7f0b50e:43b515f4c0da2167.author: Hellsten, Mark
56c7f0b50e:43b515f4c0da2167.summary: Despite growing policy interest in AI workforce development, surprisingly little is known about what defines these workers, or indeed if they differ from their occupational peers. Using a novel matched vacancy-hire dataset linking Swedish job postings to the individuals hired to fill them, drawn from register data on the entire Swedish population, I study the characteristics of workers who develop and apply AI. Observable traits including high cognitive ability, a tertiary degree in STEM subjects, and a recent migrant background largely explain occupational sorting. Of these, only higher education, prior AI experience, and a science degree set them apart within occupation. I then use earnings as a window onto unobservable differences: AI workers earn approximately 5% more than their peers, entirely explained by firm-level wages. However, AI workers with a doctorate degree stand out sharply in both traits and earnings, indicating that AI workers split into segments that differ by the complexity of their skills and tasks. Taken together, these results point to two distinct policy levers: the supply of average AI workers, termed AI integrators, can be expanded via STEM education participation, while the elite AI developers are supplied by researchers moving to the private sector.

56c7f0b50e:2b9a4702799478ba.title: The Impacts of Unauthorized Immigration on U.S. Labor and Housing Markets: New Evidence from Administrative Microdata
56c7f0b50e:2b9a4702799478ba.author: Xiaoqing Zhou
56c7f0b50e:2b9a4702799478ba.summary: From early 2021 through early 2024, the U.S. experienced an unprecedented boom in unauthorized immigration, with substantial heterogeneity across local economies. Using administrative microdata, we construct new measures of national and local unauthorized immigration flows and exploit exogenous variation using multiple empirical designs. Unauthorized immigrant worker flows increased local employment approximately one-for-one, with mixed evidence of wage depression. They also raised house prices and rents without expanding housing supply. Finally, these flows reduced labor income per capita and government transfers. These findings help inform debates surrounding how unauthorized immigration impacts labor and housing markets and public finances in the U.S.

56c7f0b50e:f54a3feb3c0de2a2.title: Job Characteristics That Matter for Women : Evidence from a Large-Scale Experiment in Pakistan
56c7f0b50e:f54a3feb3c0de2a2.author: Tas, Emcet Oktay
56c7f0b50e:f54a3feb3c0de2a2.summary: In the presence of gender-specific barriers, certain workplace environments and amenities may be particularly important for women, yet difficult to observe during job search due to information frictions. A large-scale field experiment on Pakistan's online job board publicized these job characteristics—namely, supervisor gender, coworker gender composition, work flexibility, commuting support, and overnight travel requirements. Information on these characteristics was randomly disclosed in job advertisements and email alerts. Analysis at the job-alert level shows that female jobseekers respond to supervisor gender, remote work, and commuting support. At the job level, when these characteristics were disclosed, the number of female applicants increased as the jobs were more favorable to women.

4bca44730b:e00b3f3b66af829c.title: Update: Botta v. PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, Case 3:18-cv-02615-RS

4bca44730b:e00b3f3b66af829c.summary: A judge denied PwC's motion for summary judgement. The case goes to trial in October. 0cf31f7a1a:e1807702d879be69.title: Private enforcement of competition law
0cf31f7a1a:e1807702d879be69.author: OECD
0cf31f7a1a:e1807702d879be69.summary: Private enforcement of competition law complements public enforcement and enables those harmed by anti-competitive conduct to seek compensation. Over the past decade, several jurisdictions have reformed their legal frameworks for competition damages claims, leading to increased litigation. This paper reviews these developments and examines the main legal and practical factors that affect whether claims can be brought effectively. These include follow-on and stand-alone actions, access to evidence, standing, causation, the quantification of harm and collective redress. The paper also looks at how public and private enforcement interact and the different ways in which competition authorities may support private claims, including through assistance to courts, guidance, advocacy and support for public-sector claims. The paper highlights the differences between national systems and considers how procedural design can affect access to compensation and the nature of private competition litigation.

0cf31f7a1a:33bb86fa406c50a0.title: Exploitative conduct
0cf31f7a1a:33bb86fa406c50a0.author: OECD
0cf31f7a1a:33bb86fa406c50a0.summary: Recent years have seen renewed interest in exploitative abuses under competition law, an area that has traditionally attracted less enforcement attention than exclusionary conduct. While excessive pricing has long been the principal focus of the enforcement and policy debate in this area, interest has increasingly expanded to non-price forms of exploitative conduct, including data-related exploitation and the impositions of unfair trading conditions. This paper examines how exploitative abuse is understood, assessed and addressed across jurisdictions. It considers the principal arguments for and against enforcement, compares the legal frameworks used to address the underlying conduct, and examines the analytical approaches emerging from enforcement practice.

0cf31f7a1a:29ca41aefe94d1e4.title: Gender Identity and Recorded Offending: Evidence from Linked Population Data
0cf31f7a1a:29ca41aefe94d1e4.author: Alexander Plum
0cf31f7a1a:29ca41aefe94d1e4.summary: Population evidence on gender identity and offending remains scarce. We link New Zealand’s 2023 Census to administrative records for 170, 775 New Zealand-born individuals from the 1993–1998 birth cohorts. Separate measures of sex at birth and gender distinguish six groups: cisgender women, cisgender men, transgender women, transgender men, and nonbinary individuals grouped by sex assigned at birth. Their histories of selected Police-recorded interpersonal and victim-related offenses are examined over a common ten-year window at ages 17–26. Adjusting for ethnicity, parental income, parental sentencing history, and year-month of birth, all four gender-minority groups have significantly lower odds of a qualifying record than cisgender men. For transgender women, the adjusted probability is 5.1%, compared with 12.2% for cisgender men and 6.0% for cisgender women. The corresponding differences are −7.2 and −1.0 percentage points; only the former is statistically significant. Across the main analyses of offense type, court action, victim characteristics, and location, transgender women consistently have lower adjusted probabilities than cisgender men, while differences from cisgender women are not statistically significant. These findings document variation in recorded offending obscured by conventional binary classifications.

0cf31f7a1a:03f920861f8c1bad.title: Costly Misdemeanours: Labour Market Effects of Low-Level Drink-Driving Violations
0cf31f7a1a:03f920861f8c1bad.author: Alexander Plum
0cf31f7a1a:03f920861f8c1bad.summary: This paper estimates the causal effect of a drink-driving conviction on labour market outcomes. Using linked administrative data and variation in the timing of first convictions in a staggered difference-in-differences design, we compare individuals before and after conviction to those convicted later. We find employment falls by 6–7 percentage points and monthly earnings decline by around 2 percent. The effects are driven primarily by reduced job entry as opposed to job loss. Employment effects are largest in industries where employers are more likely to screen applicants for criminal convictions.

0cf31f7a1a:996325d3194ef715.title: External Shocks and Police Behaviour: Evidence from Terrorist Attacks in the UK
0cf31f7a1a:996325d3194ef715.author: Gennaro Rossi
0cf31f7a1a:996325d3194ef715.summary: Shocks, such as terrorist attacks, may shift policing through profiling (group-targeted enforcement driven by salience) or operational changes. We test these channels using administrative data from Londonâ€™s Metropolitan Police Service on use-of-force incidents and stop-and-searches, linked to UK terrorist attacks between April 2017 and November 2019. Exploiting attack timing in a regression discontinuity-in-time design, we compare outcomes in narrow windows around each event. Across both datasets we find little evidence of short-run ethnic profiling after Muslim extremist or far-right attacks. In contrast, Muslim extremist attacks â€“ substantially more lethal in our sample â€“ are followed by a shift toward weapons searches, more public-protection-focused force, and greater use-of-force intensity for both White and Non-white subjects. The evidence is consistent with heightened alertness rather than discriminatory targeting.

0cf31f7a1a:943d59e495a01936.title: The Aftermath of the 2024 UK Riots: Reporting on Social Media, Misinformation, and Crime
0cf31f7a1a:943d59e495a01936.author: James Moir
0cf31f7a1a:943d59e495a01936.summary: On 30th July 2024, the UK saw its worst riots in over a decade following a knife attack in Southport that left three girls dead and ten injured. False claims about the attacker being a Muslim asylum seeker spread rapidly online, turning vigils into violence as far-right groups used X, TikTok and Telegram to coordinate attacks on mosques, asylum centres and local businesses. Many of the rioters received prison sentences for arson and racially aggravated offences. Information disorder played a central role in the 2024 riots, both triggering unrest and intensifying violence through the rapid dissemination of false narratives. Disinformation acted as the initial spark, later transforming into misinformation as unaware individuals reshared it. Social media sites such as Telegram involved the sharing of extremist material that merged transnational and domestic narratives. Global disinformation and local grievances became intertwined, merging foreign interference with home-grown mobilisation. As the riots took place there was evidence an online-offline feedback loop which resulted in prosecutions that relied heavily on digital evidence. This paper examines a corpus of newspaper reports on the issue of social media, disinformation, and crime in the ensuing two-year period since the riots. The news media sources were derived from a search using LexisNexis, a web-based archive of news titles in the UK. This is involved a selective search of news from the range of broadsheet and tabloid titles across the political spectrum. The key search terms were ?Stockport?, ?riots? ?social media?, ?misinformation?, ?disinformation? and ?police?. A discourse analytic approach was applied to the reports that reveal the different political stances taken on the issue of social media, misinformation, and crime. These are bound up with rhetorical constructions concerning the release of police information on the identities of alleged offenders, the control of social media, and social and…

0cf31f7a1a:61ebb4831b764bf1.title: Public salience mobilizes nationwide responses to violence against women
0cf31f7a1a:61ebb4831b764bf1.author: Gabriele Pinto
0cf31f7a1a:61ebb4831b764bf1.summary: Does public salience around femicides mobilize societal responses or trigger further harm through imitation? Using newly assembled case-level data on femicides in Italy from 2017 to 2024, we study the nationwide consequences of the most salient cases for help-seeking, police reporting, and lethal violence. We find that highly salient intimate partner femicides (IPFs) generate nationwide increases in help-seeking, and that an exceptionally salient IPF also leads to a marked rise in police reports of violence against women. Yet we find no evidence of an increase in femicides-a pattern inconsistent with copycat theories. Responses are strongest during periods of peak salience. No comparable mobilization follows a lower-salience IPF, a similarly salient femicide committed by family members, a highly salient killing of a woman not classified as a femicide, or a lower-salience falsification case. Together, these comparisons indicate that mobilization depends on salience intensity, the victim-perpetrator relationship, and the gendered nature of the violence, rather than reflecting a generic response to salient violent crime. These findings suggest that public salience can contribute to prevention strategies against gender-based violence without amplifying lethal violence.

0cf31f7a1a:7fc06c652dbd03a7.title: Debiasing Law Enforcement Officers: Evidence from an Expressive Arts Intervention in India
0cf31f7a1a:7fc06c652dbd03a7.author: María Micaela Sviatschi
0cf31f7a1a:7fc06c652dbd03a7.summary: Frontline state agents exercise substantial discretion over citizens’ access to public services, yet little is known about whether the attitudes and beliefs shaping this discretion can be changed among incumbent bureaucrats. Partnering with the Bihar Police - one of India’s largest states that operates under comparatively severe policing capacity constraints, we conduct a cluster randomized controlled trial across 417 police stations and roughly 2, 500 active duty senior field police officers to evaluate a three-day expressive arts intervention, grounded in the Theatre of the Oppressed, designed to change police responses to gender-based violence (GBV). Approximately 7 months after baseline, treated officers exhibit more favorable attitudes toward GBV, greater empathy, and stronger legal knowledge. These changes translate into observed policing behavior: in standardized victim audits conducted one year later, officers in treated stations are 15 percentage points less likely to blame victims, dismiss fewer complaints, and provide more referrals, while administrative records show a 41 percent reduction in registration delays and, over a longer horizon, increased GBV reporting by citizens. Exploiting variation generated by officer transfers, we find suggestive evidence that these effects persist when treated officers relocate and diffuse to untreated officers working alongside treated colleagues. The effects also extend to the workplace: junior female officers working with treated senior officers report lower harassment and anxiety. These findings show that the attitudes shaping bureaucratic discretion are malleable and that changing how incumbent state agents exercise authority can improve both citizen-facing service delivery and the broader workplace environment.

0cf31f7a1a:6ba77cb5cb954f9c.title: Policy Evaluation Beyond Significance Testing: Evidence from Chicago's ShotSpotter Contract
0cf31f7a1a:6ba77cb5cb954f9c.author: Adam K. Soliman
0cf31f7a1a:6ba77cb5cb954f9c.summary: Program impact estimates that are not statistically significant are often treated as providing little guidance for policy choice, even when economically important effects remain plausible. In such cases, the decision-relevant task is not simply to test whether the effect differs from zero, but to estimate the probability distribution of programmatic effects. The importance of going beyond hypothesis testing is especially clear when evaluations are underpowered relative to the effect needed for benefits to exceed costs. We illustrate this point using Chicago’s contract for ShotSpotter, an acoustical gunshot detection system that reduces police response times and may therefore have improved survival among shooting victims. Using a geographic RD design, we estimate that ShotSpotter reduced the shooting fatality rate by 2.5 percentage points, equivalent to roughly 49 fewer deaths per year. Although the estimate is not statistically significant, its implied benefit far exceeds the cost of the service. To have enough statistical power under the hypothesis testing approach to detect an effect of this size would require 87 years’ worth of Chicago shooting data. We instead implement a decision-relevant perspective using Bayesian analysis, treating the life-saving effect as a random variable. We find positive expected net benefits, with posterior probabilities that benefits exceed costs ranging from 70% under a flat prior and a $0.5 million value of statistical life to 99.6% under a no-harm prior and a $13.6 million value. The results illustrate how reliance on statistical significance can discard decision-relevant evidence when economically meaningful effects are difficult to detect precisely.

0cf31f7a1a:b34885efce18c31f.title: Unlawful Tariffs: Incidence, Damages, and Remedies
0cf31f7a1a:b34885efce18c31f.author: Gunner Heins
0cf31f7a1a:b34885efce18c31f.summary: In Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, the Supreme Court held that the tariffs imposed by executive order pursuant to the International Emergency Economic Powers Act exceeded presidential authority. The decision has generated over two thousand lawsuits and potential refund exposure in the range of $130–175 billion. This Article provides a law and economics analysis of the recovery problem. Drawing on the Bigelow measure of antitrust damages and standard tax incidence theory, the Article argues that both importers and foreign exporters have suffered cognizable injury. The damage suffered by each class depends on the incidence of the tariff, which is determined by the elasticities of domestic import demand and foreign export supply. The Article examines the complications introduced by market power, supply-chain pass-on under Illinois Brick, the problem of windfalls, and the econometric challenges of estimating the but-for price. Methodological approaches—including before-and-after comparisons, yardstick methods, and structural demand estimation—are evaluated. The Article also addresses the social welfare loss not captured by private damage claims and the procedural constraint imposed by the 180-day customs protest period.

0cf31f7a1a:a566b75bcbf21f4a.title: Large Language Models and Ottoman Court Records: Long-Term Change and Regional Comparison
0cf31f7a1a:a566b75bcbf21f4a.author: Metin M. Cosgel
0cf31f7a1a:a566b75bcbf21f4a.summary: Large language models offer new ways to turn historical texts into quantitative evidence, but their value depends on whether the resulting data support reliable comparisons. I examine that potential through Ottoman court registers, a source for studying long-term change and regional variation after regular tax surveys ceased around 1600. I combine rule-based extraction with large language models to convert 385 transcribed volumes from twelve districts into a dataset of 160, 395 entries. Rules extract formulaic information, while models classify documents, identify participants’ roles, and interpret legal outcomes. Validation uses hand-coded samples and comparisons with three published Istanbul studies of intergenerational persistence of social standing, foreign-coin use, and the decisive oath in litigation. The new extraction recovers their principal patterns and adds later observations to the standing and oath series. Applying common definitions across districts reveals different relationships between the capital and the provinces. The oath’s early seventeenth-century peak and subsequent decline appear broadly across the observed courts. Foreign silver accounted for substantial shares of recorded transaction value earlier in Antep, Amasya, and Kayseri than in Istanbul and several western and central districts. The early seventeenth-century decline in father–son status persistence in Istanbul was shared by Bursa but was not a general provincial pattern. Uneven transcription coverage, selection into court, and extraction error limit these comparisons. Within those limits, the method makes published court records usable for comparative quantitative history across several centuries and regions.

0cf31f7a1a:7949a1598c71270e.title: Education and Crime Prevention: Impacts, Mechanisms, and Policy Implications for Latin America and the Caribbean
0cf31f7a1a:7949a1598c71270e.author: Alvarez Rojas, Angelica Del Pilar
0cf31f7a1a:7949a1598c71270e.summary: Drawing on evidence from a broad range of policies and interventions including compulsory schooling reforms, improvements in school quality, early childhood education, extended school days, extracurricular programs, summer employment programs, and conditional cash transfers this paper systematically reviews the causal evidence on the relationship between education and crime to inform policy design in Latin America and the Caribbean. The review covers 81 studies and organizes the evidence into nine categories of educational policies and programs. It compares effects across crime outcomes, examines the mechanisms through which the interventions operate, and, when possible, summarizes their costs and cost-effectiveness. Overall, educational interventions tend to reduce criminal involvement, although their effectiveness varies substantially across policies and outcomes. The literature points to multiple mechanisms beyond the traditional channels of higher opportunity costs of crime and incapacitation, including socio-emotional skill development, peer effects, and household dynamics. However, relatively few studies examine the economic returns to educational interventions or incorporate crime-reduction benefits into cost-benefit analyses, which may lead to an underestimation of their social value. Finally, the evidence base is heavily concentrated in the United States, highlighting the need for more rigorous research in underrepresented regions and greater attention to contextual factors that may influence policy effectiveness. The paper concludes with policy recommendations for the region, emphasizing implementation conditions, targeting criteria, and priorities for future research.

0cf31f7a1a:7a4c906be75b9114.title: Demystifying Unconscionability: A Historical and Empirical Analysis
0cf31f7a1a:7a4c906be75b9114.author: McCall, Brian M.
0cf31f7a1a:7a4c906be75b9114.summary: The doctrine of unconscionability is encrusted with myths. First-year law students are taught that the doctrine was created in the twentieth century. Unconscionability is often presented as a novel one, born in the Uniform Commercial Code’s adoption of Section 2-302 in the mid-twentieth century. Even those scholars who are willing to look a bit further afield than the twentieth century for the origins of the unconscionability doctrine typically only reach the mid-eighteenth century. In addition to myths surrounding its origin, the doctrine has been presented as a dangerously vague and imprecise concept. Commentators and scholars have likewise characterized the doctrine as a license for courts to refuse, unpredictably and arbitrarily, to enforce some contracts. Some claim its application has the potential to destroy all of contract law. Beyond the fearmongering myths, another standard myth taught to first-year law students is that to succeed on a claim of unconscionability a party must offer at least some proof of both procedural and substantive unconscionability. This Article will thus attempt to dispel the following three myths about unconscionability: • It is a new, modern doctrine of law, • Its application is unpredictable and arbitrary, and • To prevail a party must prove both procedural and substantive unconscionability. The best way to dispel myths is through facts. This Article attempts to clear the clouds of confusion and fear surrounding the doctrine by turning to historical and empirical fact. Part I of this Article looks to the ancient past and finds that the idea that justice, and hence the law, should grant a remedy to at least some people who enter into inequitable bargains, is as old as philosophizing about justice itself (and certainly older than the mid-eighteenth century). Rather than a dangerous modern innovation, this principle of justice has ancient philosophical roots in Aristotle and ancient legal roots in Roman law. Part II of the Article…

0cf31f7a1a:442c40e658a78fd6.title: When Crime Enters City Hall: Organized Crime and Municipal Finance in Mexico
0cf31f7a1a:442c40e658a78fd6.author: Cesar Velazquez
0cf31f7a1a:442c40e658a78fd6.summary: Criminal organizations can affect local state capacity not only through violence but also through their interaction with local governments. This article examines whether criminal presence affects municipal public finances. Using 24 years of public finance data for the universe of Mexican municipalities and an event-study design, we exploit the timing of the first recorded presence of a criminal organization. We find that criminal presence is associated with lower unearmarked expenditures, driven particularly by a decline in absolute public investment and its share of total expenditure. Although the budget shares allocated to general services, personnel services, and transfers and subsidies increase, these changes do not necessarily reflect increases in absolute spending. We find no evidence of a change in own-source revenues, except in municipalities where only newly created criminal organizations are present, which exhibit higher own-source revenues. The contraction in expenditure is concentrated in municipalities with high criminal fragmentation and in those where historical criminal organizations are present. Overall, the findings indicate that organized crime is associated with a contraction in municipal expenditure and a change in budget composition.

0cf31f7a1a:867a5d651b803e1b.title: Dismissing Human Trafficking: Forced Arbitration of Survivors’ Civil Suits
0cf31f7a1a:867a5d651b803e1b.author: Werner, Daniel
0cf31f7a1a:867a5d651b803e1b.summary: For more than two decades, federal law has provided trafficked individuals the right to sue their traffickers in court and hundreds of survivors have filed suit. Their litigation has yielded millions in judgments and settlements, public accountability, development of the law, and a deeper understanding of human trafficking. Forced arbitration of human trafficking claims threatens these successes. Much has been written about the existence and enforcement of pre-dispute arbitration clauses, particularly in employment and consumer matters. This Article is the first to assess these pervasive contractual provisions in the context of human trafficking. It sets out the public and private functions of the federal private right of action for trafficking survivors. Informed by federal cases where alleged traffickers successfully compelled arbitration, the Article details how these important functions are undermined by forced arbitration and how the harms of human trafficking are exacerbated by it. Compelling arbitration of survivors’ civil claims erodes government efforts to combat human trafficking and to support survivors. This Article makes two recommendations to address this deepening and underappreciated problem. First, Congress should amend the Federal Arbitration Act (FAA) to invalidate pre-dispute arbitration provisions in cases involving human trafficking. Second, the regulations governing temporary work visas for foreign nationals should prohibit pre-dispute arbitration provisions in their employment contracts. In the meantime, survivors can continue to challenge these provisions in court using contract defenses.

0cf31f7a1a:a19e9526bcbbffbf.title: First-Month Check-Ins as an Early Indicator in Pretrial Supervision
0cf31f7a1a:a19e9526bcbbffbf.author: Warren, Madeline
0cf31f7a1a:a19e9526bcbbffbf.summary: Pretrial supervision has a short window to keep a person on track to resolve their case without returning to jail, and most of what agencies use to set supervision intensity is fixed at booking. Published pretrial research has found static factors such as criminal history and prior failures to appear more predictive than dynamic ones (Bechtel, Lowenkamp, & Holsinger, 2011), but the findings reported here may challenge that conclusion. This paper asks whether something RePath records from the first day of supervision, the share of scheduled app check-ins a participant completes in the first 30 days, says anything about how the case ends. We examined Missouri pretrial cases across 65 agencies that closed successfully or unsuccessfully between October 1, 2025 and September 30, 2026 and were open at least 30 days (4, 833 closures). Among the 1, 504 cases with check-ins scheduled in the first month, participants whose cases closed successfully had completed 68.9% of them and those whose cases closed unsuccessfully 47.3%, a gap of 21.6 points (95% CI 17.2 to 26.0; Cohen's d = 0.67). Participants who completed fewer than half closed unsuccessfully 32.9% of the time, against 14.2% for the rest (risk ratio 2.31). The unsuccessful-closure rate was highest among participants who completed little or none of their first-month check-ins (39.5% at zero) and lowest among those who completed nearly all of them (7.9% at 90–99%; none of 26 at 100%), and first-month completion separated outcomes with an AUC of .69 (95% CI .66 to .72), within the range reported for two validated pretrial risk tools, the Public Safety Assessment (.55–.68) and the federal Pretrial Risk Assessment (.67–.73), though the populations, outcomes and timing differ. The gap held across case-length floors, within agencies, and with excluded closures recoded either way. We report the result with its boundaries: one state, one year, outcomes as provided by agencies, technical revocations and new arrests not…

daedf173a6:5837cc1a37eb765f.summary: A federal grand jury in Bowling Green returned an indictment charging a Greensburg man with one count of conspiracy and eight counts of crop insurance fraud.

daedf173a6:c183c5328d359742.title: Russian National Pleads Guilty to Evading Economic Sanctions on Russia
daedf173a6:c183c5328d359742.summary: Alexander Suvorov, 52, a Russian national formerly residing in Sweden, pleaded guilty today to conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act (ECRA).

daedf173a6:5c2ce832dc49bf04.title: Peruvian National Extradited for Overseeing a Transnational Scheme to Impersonate Government Officials and Defraud U.S. Consumers
daedf173a6:5c2ce832dc49bf04.summary: Karount Jannet Toledo Vazquez, 49, of Lima, Peru, was extradited to the United States and made her initial appearance in Miami federal court to face charges for her role in operating a large fraud and extortion scheme. Toledo was arrested on Oct. 21 by Peruvian authorities pursuant to a U.S. extradition request.

daedf173a6:12e087c6a9657700.title: Chinese Tech Giant Huawei and Subsidiaries Convicted of Sanctions Violations, Fraud, Conspiracy to Steal Trade Secrets, and Money Laundering
daedf173a6:12e087c6a9657700.summary: A federal jury in the Eastern District of New York returned guilty verdicts following a three-month trial against Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. (Huawei) and three of its subsidiaries for violating U.S. sanctions involving Iran, lying to banks, money laundering, and stealing trade secrets from American companies.

daedf173a6:e6b4aaddd9e3541d.title: New York Father and Son Plead Guilty in $600M Covid Tax Fraud Scheme
daedf173a6:e6b4aaddd9e3541d.summary: A New York father and his son pleaded guilty in federal court for their roles in a conspiracy to defraud the United States of more than $600 million by filing more than 8,000 fraudulent tax returns claiming COVID-19-related employment tax credits.

daedf173a6:e678d934f0905f8b.title: Four Family Members, Including Two Chinese Nationals, Charged in $55M Medicare and Medicaid Pharmacy Fraud Scheme
daedf173a6:e678d934f0905f8b.summary: A federal grand jury in the Eastern District of New York returned an indictment on Nov. 20 charging Zhang Huang, also known as “Danny Huang,” 35, Yanle Huang, also known as “Logan Wong,” 38, Jian Xin Huang, 62, and Xiuqin Huang, 61, all of Queens, New York, variously with conspiring to bill Medicare and New York Medicaid for medically unnecessary prescription medications and paying illegal kickbacks, money laundering, and tax offenses. The defendants were previously charged by complaint with conspiracy to pay health care kickbacks on Sept. 30. Jian Xin Huang and Xiuqin Huang are Chinese nationals with lawful permanent residency in the United States.

daedf173a6:47c5db968e8cbc39.title: Justice Department Announces Largest-Ever Crackdown on Scammers, Targeting Over 800 Defendants to Protect Americans from Fraud

daedf173a6:0cd36717c0ad4097.title: 9 Illegal Aliens from Venezuela Sentenced for Roles in Nashville Sex Trafficking Organization as Part of Homeland Security Task Force Initiative
daedf173a6:0cd36717c0ad4097.summary: The last of nine illegal aliens from Venezuela were sentenced after they pleaded guilty to human trafficking and alien smuggling charges related to a sex trafficking ring that operated in several motels across Nashville, Tennessee. These defendants were sentenced in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee.

daedf173a6:7ef8ba3987c1254a.title: Federal Court Dismisses Second and Third Challenges to National Security Exemption for Energy Development in Gulf of America
daedf173a6:7ef8ba3987c1254a.summary: On Friday, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia dismissed a second lawsuit challenging the Endangered Species Committee’s national security exemption for oil and gas activities in the Gulf of America, and today it dismissed a third. The ruling follows the same court’s November 16 dismissal of a parallel challenge brought by another environmental group. In both opinions, the court again held that only the federal courts of appeals may hear challenges to the Committee's exemption decisions.

daedf173a6:be8a5a1d4b03ce46.title: United States Files Action to Recover More Than $1 Billion in Cryptocurrency Assets Stolen by North Korean Cyber Actors in Binance Hack
daedf173a6:be8a5a1d4b03ce46.summary: Today, the Justice Department announced actions taken to forfeit over $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency that was criminally obtained by North Korean actors from Binance last month. This is part of the greater government effort to assist Binance in recovering over $6 billion in stolen assets.

daedf173a6:6667105e4c206546.title: ISIS Supporter Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for Concealing His Role in Creating and Disseminating Terrorist Propaganda Via Social Media
daedf173a6:6667105e4c206546.summary: Anas Said, 30, of Houston, Texas, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison and lifetime supervised release for concealing material support to a foreign terrorist organization and making false statements to the FBI.

daedf173a6:98813f61a4fa5b9c.title: North Carolina Return Preparers Sentenced to Prison in Pandemic-Relief Fraud Scheme
daedf173a6:98813f61a4fa5b9c.summary: Two North Carolina women were sentenced to prison for conspiring to prepare false tax returns claiming fraudulent refunds based on COVID-19 tax credits.

daedf173a6:d802053156c2bb31.title: Artifact Spotlight: A Morning Suit That Made History
daedf173a6:d802053156c2bb31.summary: The formality of the Supreme Court is unmistakable, from the marble columns to the burgundy velvet curtains, every detail reinforces the gravity of the institution. But few traditions capture this sense of dignity quite like the morning suit worn by the Solicitor General when arguing before the nation's highest court.

daedf173a6:aff5c69964ebd888.title: Florida Doctor and Medical Research Employees Convicted of Falsifying Data in Clinical Trials of New Drug Treatments
daedf173a6:aff5c69964ebd888.summary: A federal jury in the Southern District of Florida convicted a medical doctor and three staff members of Pines Care Research Center LLC (Pines Care), a medical research center in Florida, for their roles in a scheme to falsify data in clinical trials of prospective new drug treatments. A fourth staff member previously pleaded guilty.

daedf173a6:d835e041e3d82fc7.title: Department of Justice Announces Nearly $150 Million to Hire Over 1,000 Law Enforcement Officers and Deputies
daedf173a6:d835e041e3d82fc7.summary: Through the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS Office), the Department of Justice today announced it has awarded nearly $150 million under the 2026 COPS Hiring Program (CHP). CHP is a competitive grant program that provides funding directly to state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies to pay for the entry-level salaries and fringe benefits of newly hired and rehired full-time sworn officers/deputies to make America safe again.

daedf173a6:58918f75704c61f9.title: Adult Day Care Owner Sentenced to 15 Months in Prison for Medicare Fraud
daedf173a6:58918f75704c61f9.summary: An adult day care owner was sentenced today to 15 months in prison for her role in billing Medicare over $500,000 for psychotherapy services that were not provided to patients.

daedf173a6:69c4aebb38720abe.title: Justice Department Files Final Condemnation to Effect Land Transfer from Arizona to Hopi Tribe
daedf173a6:69c4aebb38720abe.summary: Today, the Justice Department and Department of the Interior announced the filing of a “friendly condemnation” to effect the transfer of around 45,000 acres of land from the State of Arizona to the United States to be held in trust for the Hopi Tribe. Upon the Hopi Tribe depositing $8.2 million in the registry of the U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona as the estimate of just compensation, title to the land will pass from Arizona to the United States. Interior will then immediately place the lands into trust for the Hopi Tribe.

daedf173a6:0bfa41f309256ae4.title: Senior Leader of the Sinaloa Cartel and One of FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives Arrested in Mexico Following a Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
daedf173a6:0bfa41f309256ae4.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores , also known as “Chapo Isidro,” an alleged leader of the Sinaloa Cartel, has been captured by the Mexican military following a Homeland Security Task Force Investigation.

daedf173a6:1667609fd222c038.title: Indian National Sentenced to Over 19 Years in Prison for Plotting to Assassinate U.S. Citizen In New York City
daedf173a6:1667609fd222c038.summary: Nikhil Gupta, also known as “Nick,” 55, an Indian national, was sentenced today to 235 months in prison for his participation in a scheme directed by a government of India employee to assassinate an attorney and political activist in the United States. In February 2026, Gupta pled guilty to a superseding indictment charging him with murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

daedf173a6:460655ecdca1b958.title: DOJ Scores Key Victory in Precedent-Setting Military Attorney Licensing Case
daedf173a6:460655ecdca1b958.summary: The Justice Department has defeated New Mexico’s attempt to dismiss a landmark case involving the licensing of servicemember and military spouse attorneys. On Nov. 19, Judge Kea Riggs of the U.S. District for the District of New Mexico denied motions to dismiss filed by the New Mexico Supreme Court and the New Mexico Board of Bar Examiners in the Department’s first-ever lawsuit to enforce the professional license portability provisions of the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA).

daedf173a6:97208d236ad6e319.title: Honor the Honorable: The Attorney General's Award for Distinguished Service in Policing

daedf173a6:5d7b7a7bbccabb35.title: Law Firm Owner Indicted for Willful Failure to File Tax Returns
daedf173a6:5d7b7a7bbccabb35.summary: An indictment was unsealed today in the District of Colorado charging a Colorado Springs, Colorado, man with willfully failing to file individual and corporate tax returns for the years 2020 to 2025.

daedf173a6:ad26df90d6584034.title: Justice Department Announces Recipients of Honor the Honorable: The Attorney General’s Award for Distinguished Service in Policing
daedf173a6:ad26df90d6584034.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche today announced the recipients of Honor the Honorable: The Attorney General’s Award for Distinguished Service in Policing. This award represents the Department of Justice’s reaffirmed commitment to uplifting the valor and exceptional contributions to policing of our great nation’s law enforcement personnel.

daedf173a6:7374a59a9807af0e.title: Louisiana Woman Convicted of Fraud, Obstruction, and Money Laundering in $17M Tax Refund Scheme
daedf173a6:7374a59a9807af0e.summary: A federal jury in the Western District of Louisiana convicted Jane Frances Pierce, 64, of Boyce, Louisiana, of mail fraud, filing false tax returns, corruptly interfering with an IRS investigation, and money laundering.

daedf173a6:a3b9343a93e71495.title: Northeast Georgia Man Charged with International Money Laundering and Destroying Evidence Tied to ISIS
daedf173a6:a3b9343a93e71495.summary: A Lavonia, Georgia, resident is in federal custody charged by criminal complaint with international money laundering and destruction of evidence following an FBI investigation into allegations of sending more than $26,000 to individuals and groups affiliated with a designated foreign terrorist organization, the Islamic State of Iraq and al Sham (ISIS).

daedf173a6:3637861a20c47c4c.title: Kansas Realtor Indicted for Tax Evasion, Failure to File Tax Returns, and Pandemic Relief Fraud
daedf173a6:3637861a20c47c4c.summary: A federal grand jury in Kansas City, Kansas, returned a superseding indictment yesterday charging a Louisburg, Kansas, woman with tax evasion, wire fraud, and willful failure to file personal and corporate income tax returns.

daedf173a6:0f5511f17ec02c6c.title: Michigan Home Health Care Agency Owner Sentenced to 4 Years in Prison for $1.6M Medicare Fraud Scheme Fueled by Illegal Kickbacks
daedf173a6:0f5511f17ec02c6c.summary: A Michigan nurse and home health agency owner was sentenced today to 4 years in prison for a $1.6 million scheme to defraud Medicare. She was also ordered to pay $1,652,130.67 in restitution to Medicare, and to pay $1,652,130.67 in forfeiture.

daedf173a6:641ca28fde4020d0.title: 3 Mexican Nationals Plead Guilty to Laundering Millions of Dollars in Drug Proceeds from the United States to Mexico
daedf173a6:641ca28fde4020d0.summary: Three Mexican nationals pleaded guilty for their roles in the collection of millions in drug proceeds in the United States and the return of those proceeds via cryptocurrency or wire transfers to Mexico as part of a money laundering conspiracy.

daedf173a6:e2e036de13af3eda.title: Justice Department Secures Permanent Injunction Against California Laws Restricting Federal Law Enforcement Operations
daedf173a6:e2e036de13af3eda.summary: The United States District Judge Christina A. Snyder of the United States District Court for the Central District of California entered a permanent injunction prohibiting the State of California, Gavin Newsom in his official capacity as Governor of California, and Rob Bonta in his official capacity as Attorney General of California, from enforcing California laws regulating federal law enforcement officers and agencies. The order permanently enjoins enforcement of Sections 7288 and 7289 of the California Government Code and Sections 185.5 and 13654 of the California Penal Code against the United States, federal law enforcement officers, and federal law enforcement agencies. The court entered the permanent injunction as part of a final resolution of the United States' lawsuit challenging California's unconstitutional attempt to regulate federal law enforcement operations.

daedf173a6:68fda0ebeab1cd31.title: Federal Jury Convicts Fifth Defendant for Scheme to Assassinate Haitian President Jovenel Moïse in Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
daedf173a6:68fda0ebeab1cd31.summary: A federal jury in Miami convicted a fifth defendant for his role in the July 7, 2021, assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse.

daedf173a6:d995a3598e8eea6b.title: Federal Court Dismisses Challenge to National Security Exemption for Energy Development in Gulf of America
daedf173a6:d995a3598e8eea6b.summary: The U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia dismissed a lawsuit earlier this week challenging the first national security exemption ever issued pursuant to the Endangered Species Act. The exemption terminated litigation threatening oil and gas in the Gulf of America — a critical source of domestic production. The court held that it lacked jurisdiction because Congress directed all challenges to the Committee’s exemption decisions to the federal courts of appeals, not the district courts.

daedf173a6:11ad855909f3ca1f.title: Justice Department’s Statement on the Closing of Its Investigation of NextEra’s Acquisition of Dominion
daedf173a6:11ad855909f3ca1f.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice issued the following statement today in connection with the closing of the Antitrust Division’s investigation into the acquisition of Dominion Energy Inc. (Dominion) by NextEra Energy Inc. (NextEra) (together, “the Parties”):

daedf173a6:d082bc03e4a8fec8.title: Pharmacy Owner Sentenced to 82 Months in Prison for $5.6M Health Care Fraud Scheme and Illegal Distribution of Oxycodone
daedf173a6:d082bc03e4a8fec8.summary: A Michigan pharmacy owner was sentenced yesterday to 82 months in prison with three years’ supervised release for a $5.6 million health care fraud scheme and for illegally distributing oxycodone. The defendant has been detained since October 7, after his arrest for violating his bond conditions.

daedf173a6:5a35d6741a6c0577.title: Peruvian National Sentenced in Transnational Government Imposter Scheme that Defrauded Thousands of U.S. Consumers
daedf173a6:5a35d6741a6c0577.summary: Carla Magaly Alcedo Mendoza (Alcedo), 45, of Lima, Peru, was sentenced today to eight years in prison and three years of supervised release for overseeing a years-long transnational fraud conspiracy that used government impersonation tactics to defraud thousands of consumers across the United States.

daedf173a6:ada911e42e1176b3.title: “Lows” Gang Member Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison For His Participation in a RICO Conspiracy
daedf173a6:ada911e42e1176b3.summary: A federal judge sentenced Deontae Jackson, 37, of Minneapolis to 10 years in prison for his role in a Racketeering Influenced Corrupt Organization (RICO) conspiracy that included violence and fentanyl distribution.

daedf173a6:9429077781585274.title: Texas-Based Company Pleads Guilty to Trafficking Deadly Synthetic Opioids
daedf173a6:9429077781585274.summary: A business-to-business online marketplace headquartered in Texas — eWorldTrade LLC — pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute synthetic opioids for unlawful importation into the United States and agreed to pay a criminal fine of $1,350,000 based on its ability to pay.

daedf173a6:9b1a246b99073e69.title: Maryland Man Sentenced to 27 Years in Prison for Sex Trafficking Two Adult Women
daedf173a6:9b1a246b99073e69.summary: Brandon Sartor, 33, of Prince George’s County, Maryland, was sentenced to 27 years in prison and ordered to pay $239,800 in restitution for sex trafficking two adult women using force, fraud, or coercion.

daedf173a6:7c0a9602aaf493e9.title: Russian National Indicted for Acting as a Foreign Agent of Russia to Target Silicon Valley Technology and Defense Company
daedf173a6:7c0a9602aaf493e9.summary: A federal grand jury has indicted Igor D’iu, a Russian national, on charges of conspiring to act as an agent of a foreign government, acting as an agent of a foreign government without notice to the Attorney General, interstate stalking, and fraud in connection with identification documents, all in connection with an alleged scheme to conduct surveillance and gather information about employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company.

daedf173a6:19ac5cbcaa2aeeed.title: Mississippi Businessman Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for $19M Medicare Fraud
daedf173a6:19ac5cbcaa2aeeed.summary: A Mississippi businessman was sentenced yesterday to 10 years in prison for paying illegal kickbacks for fraudulent doctors’ orders and then using those orders to fraudulently bill Medicare over $19 million through seven different durable medical equipment (DME) supply companies.

daedf173a6:08260c4e506ca9b4.title: Justice Department, VA, and VA OIG Announce Enforcement Actions Against 15 Defendants for Defrauding Veterans Benefits Programs
daedf173a6:08260c4e506ca9b4.summary: The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, along with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and VA Office of Inspector General today announced a nationwide series of enforcement actions targeting VA benefit fraud and related offenses amid National Veterans Awareness Week.

daedf173a6:ce9591bac2eeda69.title: Salinas Man Sentenced to Over 11 Years in Prison for Attempted Sexual Exploitation of a 12-Year-Old and Distributing Child Pornography
daedf173a6:ce9591bac2eeda69.summary: Donald Ramirez, 40, of Salinas, California, was sentenced to 138 months in prison and 15 years of supervised release for attempted enticement and coercion of a minor and for distribution of child pornography. He was also ordered to pay $72,000 in restitution.

daedf173a6:ef0c19fcf32db5fc.title: PACE Organization InnovAge Agrees to Pay $36M to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations of Failing to Provide Comprehensive Medical Services and Timely Specialist Referrals to Seniors
daedf173a6:ef0c19fcf32db5fc.summary: InnovAge Holding Corporation (InnovAge), headquartered in Denver, Colorado, has agreed to pay a total of $36 million to resolve allegations that it violated the federal False Claims Act and state laws by failing to provide required comprehensive medical services and timely referrals to medical specialists as expeditiously as its patients’ health conditions required.

daedf173a6:39101bd7320a5dfa.title: JOINT STATEMENT FROM DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE AND DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE ON MEGASPEED INVESTIGATION
daedf173a6:39101bd7320a5dfa.summary: The Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice are providing the public with an update on the investigation of the Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has attracted significant public attention in the last week. While we don’t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting.

daedf173a6:2bf70a5ca566a9ba.title: Justice Department Surpasses $1B In Awards Under Reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act
daedf173a6:2bf70a5ca566a9ba.summary: The Justice Department announced today that it has awarded more than $1 billion in compassionate compensation to newly eligible claimants under the recently reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act (RECA).

daedf173a6:b69b10110a62ec05.title: Iranian Intelligence Agent Sentenced to Over 27 Years in Prison for Foiled Plot to Assassinate U.S. Government Officials
daedf173a6:b69b10110a62ec05.summary: Earlier today, in federal court in Brooklyn, Asif Merchant, 48, of Pakistan, was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Eric R. Komitee to 330 months in prison for attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries and murder for hire.

daedf173a6:837ec87a40e5adb5.title: Tajik National Convicted of Providing Material Support to ISIS and Firearms Offenses
daedf173a6:837ec87a40e5adb5.summary: A federal jury in Brooklyn today convicted Mansuri Manuchekhri, also known as “Mansuri Manchekhri” and “Manysher,” on four counts of an indictment charging him with conspiring to provide material support to the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham (ISIS) and the Islamic State-Khorasan Province (ISIS-K), conspiring to possess and possessing firearms and ammunition while unlawfully in the United States, and making false statements to federal agents.

daedf173a6:68c271f878b3434e.title: Child Predator Deemed “Extreme Danger” Sentenced to Life in Prison For Relentlessly Sexually Exploiting Multiple Minors in Hawaii
daedf173a6:68c271f878b3434e.summary: Darren Patrick Riley, 46, of Honolulu, Hawaii, was sentenced to life in prison by Senior U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright following his conviction by a jury of 12 counts related to his trafficking and sexual exploitation of five minor boys in Oahu in 2019 and 2020.

daedf173a6:50013f344d0eb5d3.title: Alleged Member of “8-Digits Team” Ransomware Group Extradited from Italy for Role in Major Data Extortion Campaign Against U.S. Hospitals, Healthcare Entities, and Schools
daedf173a6:50013f344d0eb5d3.summary: Roman Khlynovskiy, 43, a Kazak national, made his initial appearance in Knoxville, Tennessee, federal court today after being extradited from Italy to face charges for his alleged role in a ransomware and extortion conspiracy that targeted U.S. schools, hospitals, and healthcare entities.

daedf173a6:02229e9001c07f37.title: Former Honduran Consul General Charged and 3 Others Arrested in Alleged Bribery and Money Laundering Scheme
daedf173a6:02229e9001c07f37.summary: Ada Evila Serrano Nuñez (Ada Serrano), the former Consul General of the Honduran Consulate in Atlanta, was arrested in Atlanta on charges alleging her participation in a bribery and money laundering scheme. The indictment, which was unsealed after her arrest, includes one count of conspiracy to violate the Foreign Extortion Prevention Act (FEPA), one count of violating FEPA, and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering.

daedf173a6:83c9b0701e7621e0.title: Introduction to Federal Firearm Rights Restoration

daedf173a6:742acb1d2e68f205.title: Chiropractor and Former CEO Sentenced for Using Abusive Tax Shelter
daedf173a6:742acb1d2e68f205.summary: A Puerto Rico chiropractor, formerly of Westmont, Illinois, was sentenced last week to 15 months in prison for filing a false tax return in connection with his use of an illegal tax shelter. He was additionally sentenced to one year of supervised release and ordered to pay restitution of $1,295,663 and interest of $429,026.

daedf173a6:25b0b39f527964c9.title: Mexican Cartel Leader Known As “Tony Montana” Sentenced for Armed Drug Trafficking as Part of Homeland Security Task Force Initiative
daedf173a6:25b0b39f527964c9.summary: Antonio Oseguera Cervantes, 67, of Michoacán, Mexico, a career drug trafficker for several Mexican cartels, was sentenced today to 270 months in prison for international drug trafficking and firearm offenses.

daedf173a6:061efe63106afada.title: Florida Man Pleads Guilty to $42M Durable Medical Equipment and Cancer Genetic Testing Fraud on Medicare
daedf173a6:061efe63106afada.summary: A Florida man pleaded guilty today to a $42 million fraud on Medicare involving false claims for durable medical equipment (DME) and cancer genetic testing. He also pled guilty to fraudulently obtaining a Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan.

daedf173a6:4ff7330842264dd9.title: HVAC Supplier Johnson Controls Inc. and Two Subsidiaries Agree to Pay $5 Million to Settle Cybersecurity Fraud Allegations
daedf173a6:4ff7330842264dd9.summary: Johnson Controls, Inc., of Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and two subsidiaries, Johnson Controls Fire Protection LP and Johnson Controls Security Solutions LLC (collectively, “Johnson Controls”), have agreed to pay $5 million to resolve allegations that they violated the False Claims Act by failing to comply with cybersecurity requirements in their federal contracts and subcontracts for building products and services, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) services.

daedf173a6:f9b66a421ebfea46.title: Federal Court in San Diego, California, Enters Permanent Injunction Barring Criminally Prosecuted Tax Preparer from Preparing Federal Tax Returns for Others
daedf173a6:f9b66a421ebfea46.summary: The U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California has issued an order permanently barring Oladapo Olagbemi, who managed a San Diego-based tax return preparation business, from preparing federal tax returns for any person or entity other than himself, the Justice Department announced today. The injunction also bars Olagbemi from, among other things, owning any business involved in tax return preparation or training any person in the preparation of tax returns. Olagbemi consented to the civil injunction order.
